384YE Spring Equinox Imperial elections.d: The national elections returned Flávio Capra Gláucio van Holberg for Holberg, Marya Zoranova Doubek for Karsk, Myshki Marishka Letuchaya for Miekarova, Alan Sheppard for Mournwold, Ianthe for Reikos and Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra for Segura. The Senate appointed ambassadors, advisors, the Imperial Spymaster Bernard Dugdale and seven generals, as well as many market and resource stewards. The Synod filled cardinal, inquisitor and champion posts, with Clytemnestra of the House of the Wanderer becoming Cardinal of Wisdom on 288 votes. Ezro i Alvera i Erigo became Imperial Fleet Master. The Bourse auctioned and voted on its titles, including Master of the Imperial Mint, which went to Gancio for 86 thrones.

n.Highguard: Highguard's citizens elected Ianthe as Senator for Reikos.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast elected Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra as Senator for Segura.
n.The League: Flávio Capra Gláucio van Holberg was elected Senator for Holberg, giving the city a voice in the Senate.
n.The Marches: The Marches elected Alan Sheppard as Senator for Mournwold.
n.Varushka: Varushka chose two senators: Marya Zoranova Doubek for Karsk and Myshki Marishka Letuchaya for Miekarova.

t.Holberg: Holberg's new senator was Flávio Capra Gláucio van Holberg.
t.Karsk: Karsk's new senator was Marya Zoranova Doubek.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova's new senator was Myshki Marishka Letuchaya.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold's new senator was Alan Sheppard.
t.Segura: Segura's new senator was Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Senate appointed Beatrix Amalia De Rondell zu Holberg as Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market.

384YE Spring Equinox Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 2612 thrones and 2 crowns. The Senate abrogated the Moonwater Hall in Upwold and criminalised membership of, or support for, the Hand of Dumon. It changed virtue assembly membership so that priests can move between assemblies, and raised the Burning Falcon army for 250 thrones. It also commissioned an appraisal of inciting slave uprisings in Sarangrave. Commissions included the Churnspire in Peregro, the Great Harbour of Elos, Hufi's Garden, a justicar sanctuary on the Isle of the Osseini, a Grendel embassy, an Iron Roads extension into Ossium and upgraded mana ministries. Bernard Dugdale became Imperial Spymaster, and ambassadors were appointed to Otkodov, the Commonwealth, Faraden and the Sumaah Republic.

n.Dawn: Astolat's senator received 140 thrones to improve the Towerjacks with the Engineer quality. Dawnish senators also seconded several motions, including the abrogation of Moonwater Hall and the expansion of the Skarsind College of Warcasting.
n.Druj: The Senate commissioned Graciana i Lopez i Guerra to appraise using the Sarangrave spy network to incite slave uprisings and raids, aiming to cause the Druj economic and military damage.
n.Grendel: An embassy to the Grendel is to be built in Cargo for the Imperial Fleetmaster. Imperial projects were also begun in Grendel-held Spiral and Feroz. A motion to appraise Imperial captives held by the Grendel failed.
n.Highguard: Highborn senators drove several motions, including the abrogation of Moonwater Hall, the Churnspire and 50 thrones for the Academy. Accalon of Felix's Watch was elected Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Skarsind College of Warcasting gained a ministry, and its Preceptor is now chosen by the Imperial Orcs' Bourse voting style. The Legion Engineer commissioned the Twilight Demesne in Skarsind.
n.Navarr: Navarri senators secured the outlawing of the Hand of Dumon and the reform of virtue assembly membership. The Advisor on the Vallorn, Nathair Autumngale, commissioned research into the Feverwater and its docks of Terunael origin.
n.The Brass Coast: A new Freeborn army, the Burning Falcon, is to be raised, and its general will carry the Flame Rampant banner. The Master of the Koboldi, Sagua i'Ezmara, announced the improvement of the Court of the White Fountain.
n.The League: The mana ministries in Tassato, Sarvos and Temeschwar are to be upgraded for 200 thrones, and the Pelican Tower is to be built in Foracci. League citizens were elected Ambassador to the Commonwealth and Ambassador to Faraden.
n.The Marches: Bregasland received 400 thrones for resupply and the Breadbasket's prosperity, and a Bounders Hall was commissioned in Sarcombe. Upwold lost the Moonwater Hall, and Bernard Dugdale became Imperial Spymaster.
n.Thule: The Senate appointed Yevgeni Katzev of Varushka as Ambassador to Otkodov, the Empire's envoy to the Thule.
n.Urizen: Urizen gains the Churnspire in Peregro, a restored Great Harbour of Elos and an improved Court of the White Fountain. The Court's new Captain of the Fountain's Guard is to be chosen by Urizen's generals.
n.Varushka: The Ketsov family settled in Karsk around the Mir Mozga, and Ossium was given the wealth of the Lomaa in place of mine expansion. The Iron Roads are to be extended into Ossium and the Korotny docks expanded.
n.Wintermark: Hufi's Garden was commissioned, which will create the Woundbinder of the Mark, and 80 thrones went towards the Imperial Seer's scrying. The Grimnir of Wittal Grove title was kept, and the Talon of Kauppahall is now appointed by Tally of the Votes.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Towerjacks improvement and received the 140 thrones for it, and seconded the mana ministry upgrade.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Churnspire and seconded the justicar sanctuary.
t.Bregasland: Bregasland's senator received 400 thrones for military and magical resupply. The Keeper of the Breadbasket allocated the Breadbasket's prosperity to Bregasland in recognition of its people's suffering.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: its senator received 50 thrones for the Academy's training of children, and seconded funds for the Imperial Seer.
t.Feroz: A sanctuary for justicars is to be built on the Isle of the Osseini in Feroz, creating the Justicar of Osseini. The Imperial Guerdon was also assigned to the evacuation of Feroz.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed Hufi's Garden and seconded the failed motion on Lepidean True Liao.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded the outlawing of the Hand of Dumon and proposed the Imperial Spymaster's appointment.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: its senator's motion on the Butchers Bank debt was withdrawn, and Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg donated 28 thrones to the treasury.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the justicar sanctuary and seconded the Grendel embassy.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's senator received 80 thrones for the Imperial Seer's scrying. The Senate kept the Grimnir of Wittal Grove title for its healing house.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed inviting the Ketsov to establish a vale at Mir Mozga.
t.Karsk: The Ketsov family settled in Karsk around the Mir Mozga, opening dragonbone and forest resources to two titles. Pavel Novak announced an expansion of the Korotny docks, which will create the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed raising the Burning Falcon and seconded the Axos treaty.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed outlawing the Hand of Dumon and seconded the Burning Falcon.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed sharing the wealth of the Lomaa and seconded other motions.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed disseminating Lowther's Gaze and seconded the Ambassador to Faraden.
t.Morrow: A tower, the Churnspire, is to be built in Peregro and ceded to Meraud. It will create the Churnspire Adjutor, a title elected by Urizen's mages. Morrow's senator also proposed the change to the Imperial Magus title.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold's senator proposed the Bounders Hall in Sarcombe and seconded the Bregasland resupply. The Bounders Hall will create the Bailiff of the Downs.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: its senator's motion to appraise Grendel prisoners failed, and it seconded the Sumaah ambassador.
t.Ossium: Ossium gave up any expansion of the Crawling Depths in exchange for the Lomaa's wealth spreading prosperity across the territory. The Iron Roads are to be extended there, with labour costs raised by its under-developed state. The Ketsov family left Ossium to settle in Karsk.
t.Redoubt: The Great Harbour of Elos is to be restored for 300 thrones. The Court of the White Fountain is being made unbreakable, and a Captain of the Fountain's Guard will be created.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed abrogating Moonwater Hall and seconded the Imperial Magus amendment.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos's mana ministry is to be upgraded, and Achille di Sarvos announced the Pelican Tower in Foracci. Its senator also proposed the Axos treaty, which drew constitutional reservations.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed electing the Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded the abrogation of Moonwater Hall.
t.Skarsind: The Warcaster College of Skarsind gained a ministry and a new method of appointment. The Legion Engineer commissioned the Twilight Demesne mana sinecure in Skarsind.
t.Spiral: The Imperial Spymaster commissioned a unique spy network at the Spire of Oblivion's Edge, ceded to the eternal Sung. The Constitutional Court has raised a concern about it for the Summer Solstice.
t.Tassato: Tassato's mana ministry is to be upgraded as part of the Grandmaster Ministries expansion its senator proposed.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's mana ministry is to be upgraded. Its senator also proposed the Sarangrave slave uprising appraisal.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the virtue assembly reform and the Ambassador to the Commonwealth.
t.Upwold: The Faraden trade hub of Moonwater Hall in Upwold was abrogated.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Great Harbour of Elos and seconded the Iron Roads extension.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded the expansion of the Skarsind College of Warcasting.

r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: The Senate declined to abrogate the Grimnir of Wittal Grove title. The title was instead amended to state that it is intended to be held by a grimnir.
r.Morrow/Peregro: The Churnspire, a tower taller than Pakaanan's Pass, is to be built in Peregro and ceded to the eternal Meraud.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Sharing the wealth of the Lomaa removes the Underpopulated quality from the Drownbark Forest.
r.Redoubt/Naris: The Great Harbour of Elos in Naris is to be restored, which will create the Elosian Architect.
r.Sarvos/Foracci: The self-funded Pelican Tower sinecure is to be built in Foracci, creating the Custodian of the Pelican Tower.

384YE Spring Equinox interlude.d: The Imperial Guerdon stood at 350 thrones, shared among units supporting the Strong Reeds, Bloodcloaks, Summer Storm and Wolves of War. Mandates gave Highborn units cheaper upgrades, boosted Wintermark raiders and rewarded Dawnish units supporting armies engaged in Dark Ranging in Brocéliande. Veterans of Hercynia and Therunin were still recovering. Units could raid, settle or explore Ossium. Trade suffered with Asavea and Issyk, Jarmish and Iron Confederacy ports were closed, and the Commonwealth and Sarcophan Delves offered extras. Fleets could carry freed orcs out of Axos. The magistrates' hunt for followers of Yaw'nagrah cost every mana site one crystal mana, and several mandates altered congregations' votes and liao.

n.Dawn: Dawnish military units supporting Dawnish, Highborn or Navarr armies engaged in Dark Ranging gained an extra crown and two herbs until the Winter Solstice 384YE, and Dawnish congregations gained one liao and two votes under the Love, Glory, and Virtue mandate.
n.Druj: Imperial units in Ossium were offered the chance to raid Druj insurgents and their resource caches, and to bring former Druj slaves and freed human settlements into Varushka.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the temple in Grendel-held Feroz is noted as one of two Asavean temples whose presence might have offset the losses from trade sanctions.
n.Highguard: Highborn units could upgrade for one fewer wain of mithril until the Autumn Equinox 384YE. Highborn congregations gained liao and votes through cooperation with Dawn but lost two votes and one liao to the call to fight the vallorn.
n.Navarr: Units that fought to protect the Navarr territories of Hercynia and Therunin were still recovering until the Summer Solstice, and Navarr armies engaged in Dark Ranging could draw Dawnish units with extra rewards.
n.The League: Congregations in Temeschwar and Tassato gained two votes and one liao under the anti-idolatry mandate enacted by Rafael Barossa di Tassato, for as long as the Synod clearly opposes idolatry.
n.Urizen: Congregations in Redoubt gained two votes and one liao under the Reject False Gods mandate, and fourteen rituals were added to Urizen lore during the Winter Solstice.
n.Varushka: Units were invited to cement Imperial control of Ossium by raiding, settling or exploring it, and Varushkan mine and forest production rose by one rank until the Spring Equinox under Raskylov's mandate.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark units that raided the Jotun-held Pride of Ikka's Tears gained a two-rank morale bonus from Rafe's mandate, and Hahnmark congregations gained two votes and one liao.

t.Brocéliande: Although the vallorn here had become quiescent, Highborn congregations were urged to keep opposing it, and Dawnish units supporting armies engaged in Dark Ranging earned extra rewards.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the temple in Feroz is named as one of two Asavean temples that could have offset the losses from trade sanctions.
t.Hahnmark: Congregations in Hahnmark gained two votes and one liao while the Synod clearly opposes idolatry, because of the forced redesign of buildings by the Asavean architect.
t.Hercynia: Units that fought in the campaign to protect Hercynia suffered a two-rank penalty until the start of the Summer Solstice 384YE.
t.Karsk: Congregations in Karsk received four extra votes and two liao until the Spring Equinox, then the standard anti-idolatry bonus, and units settling Ossium could guard Varushkan traders heading east from Karsk.
t.Ossium: Military units could raid Druj insurgents, help freed slaves establish vales, or explore dark places and contact non-Druj orcs, each action contributing to firmer Imperial control.
t.Redoubt: Congregations in Redoubt gained two votes and one liao for as long as the Synod clearly stands against idolatry.
t.Tassato: Congregations in Tassato gained two votes and one liao for as long as the Synod clearly stands against idolatry.
t.Temeschwar: Congregations in Temeschwar gained two votes and one liao for as long as the Synod clearly stands against idolatry.
t.Therunin: Units that fought in the campaign to protect Therunin suffered a one-rank penalty until the start of the Summer Solstice 384YE.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Dawnish military units supporting Dawnish, Highborn or Navarr armies engaged in Dark Ranging gained one extra crown and two random herbs until the Winter Solstice 384YE.

384YE Spring Equinox winds of fortune.d: Feroz's borders closed after the treaty's six months, leaving many Freeborn trapped unless rescued by sea. Spiral's cooperation with the Salt Lord halted the Citadel Guard's decline. Three Highborn armies attacked in Zenith, where some two thousand freed Winter spirits lingered. Ossium became indelibly Varushkan, except the Bonewood and Webwood ceded to the Thule. Sarvos became the City of Masks, the Holmauer Gate was consecrated in Holberg, and the Lepidean University in Bastion was completed. The koboldi warned of trogoni beneath Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, requiring a Red Iron Door. Navarr marched to Liathaven seeking the Heirs of Terunael, and the Brass Coast's Tally of the Votes was opened to all fleet owners.

n.Dawn: The Highborn accepted the Dawnish gauntlet and announced a grand cathleon to conquer the Barrens, giving Dawnish priests a chance to respond, while Dawnish knights joined the settlement of Ossium.
n.Druj: Three Highborn armies returned to Zenith to drive the Druj out, and the proposed Urizen fortifications in Zenith remained largely theoretical while the Druj held it.
n.Grendel: The Grendel closed Feroz's borders, still traded through Oran and continued repatriating Imperial slaves, while cooperating warily with the Urizen of Spiral despite lingering ill feeling over traders robbed at Anvil.
n.Highguard: Three Highborn armies attacked in Zenith with unwavering Courage, and the Highborn National Assembly declared a grand cathleon for the Barrens and was due to appoint the first Lepidean Librarian in Bastion.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orcs were among the invited guests to a plenipotentiary parley, faced a Constitutional Court ruling on orc membership of the virtue assemblies, and learned how the mission to bring Axou orcs to the Empire had fared.
n.Jotun: The Marchers, aided by Navarr and Wintermark scouts, prepared a raid into Jotun-held Skallahn, and a large Navarr force set out for Jotun-held Liathaven to hunt the Heirs of Terunael.
n.Navarr: Navarr scouts helped identify raid targets in Skallahn, a large Navarr force volunteered to search Liathaven for the Heirs of Terunael, and Navarr Miaren lay near the threatened sinkhole.
n.The Brass Coast: With Feroz's borders closed, many Freeborn remained trapped awaiting an evacuation by sea, and the Tally of the Votes for Freeborn titles was changed to include all fleet owners rather than only privateers.
n.The League: Sarvos was remade as the City of Masks, Holberg saw the consecration of the Holmauer Gate, and League Temeschwar was among the territories threatened by trogoni from the sinkhole.
n.The Marches: Marcher folk prepared to take the fight to the Jotun with a raid on Skallahn, the Marcher Assembly faced a choice over the threshers, and Upwold lay near the threatened sinkhole.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Bonewood and Webwood in Ossium are noted as ceded by the Senate to the allied Thule orcs.
n.Urizen: Urizen saw fortifications appraised for all four of its territories, cooperation with the Grendel in Spiral that halted the Citadel Guard's decline, Highborn armies fighting alongside it in Zenith, and a new Broken Shore Mithril Market completed in Redoubt.
n.Varushka: Ossium became indelibly Varushkan with vales spreading across the territory, though a canker lurked in Karsk, and Varushka was named among the nations facing opportunities and challenges in Zenith.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark folk were among the invited guests to a plenipotentiary, Wintermark scouts aided the Skallahn raid, Hahnmark lay near the threatened sinkhole, and Wintermark fleets favoured the Grendel port of Oran.

t.Bastion: Work on the Lepidean University in Bastion was completed, with the first Lepidean Librarian due to be appointed and a dose of true liao made available to the Synod.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is described as lying across the Bay of Catazar from Feroz, and the Grendel are called the orcs of the Bay.
t.Feroz: The Grendel closed Feroz's borders after the six-month grace period, leaving many Imperial citizens trapped, though a spy network built with Shantarim corsair families offered a way to evacuate them.
t.Hahnmark: Part of Hahnmark was swallowed by Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, and the koboldi warned that trogoni swarming in the sinkhole could pour out at any moment.
t.Holberg: Severin Teyhard von Holberg came to Holberg with true liao to consecrate the Holmauer Gate, amid local fears that the city was cursed.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: a canker lurking in Karsk is noted as a threat the Varushkans must deal with.
t.Liathaven: A large Navarr force volunteered to go to Liathaven to test the theory that the Heirs of Terunael are based there.
t.Miaren: Part of Miaren was swallowed by Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, which the koboldi warned now hid swarming trogoni that could devastate the surrounding lands.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold's devastation by Imperial curses three years earlier is cited as the root of the thresher debate.
t.Ossium: Backed by two Imperial armies and a host of helpers, the Varushkans carved out vales across Ossium, making it indelibly Varushkan apart from the Bonewood and Webwood.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt received a surprising suggestion for increasing its Prosperity, fortifications were appraised for the Architects of Stone at Delving, and the Broken Shore Mithril Market was completed at Cargo.
t.Sarvos: With the Hag Queen's doom lifted, Sarvos became the City of Masks and was quickly gaining a reputation as the most elegant city in the known world.
t.Skallahn: Marcher raiders, guided by Navarr and Wintermark scouts, prepared to strike targets in Skallahn, with the aims yet to be chosen between military, economic and spiritual.
t.Spiral: Spiral's Urizen cautiously cooperated with the Grendel occupiers, halting the Citadel Guard's decline, though bad feeling over traders robbed at Anvil still had to be addressed.
t.Temeschwar: Part of Temeschwar was swallowed by Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, which the koboldi warned now threatened an outpouring of trogoni.
t.Upwold: Part of Upwold was swallowed by Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, and the koboldi warned that trogoni swarming below could devastate it.
t.Zenith: Three Highborn armies attacked the Druj in Zenith, where some two thousand freed Winter spirits remained, and fortifications proposed for the territory were largely theoretical.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: The six months the Grendel treaty allowed Imperial citizens to leave Afarjasse expired and the borders closed, leaving those remaining trapped without outside help.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: The six-month window for Imperial citizens to leave Morajasse ended with the borders closed, making rescue by sea the only way out.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The formerly Imperial port of Oran, now wholly under Grendel control, stayed open to Imperial fleets and proved especially popular with Wintermark captains.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: The Holmauer Gate was consecrated with true liao, accompanied by powerful spiritual events intended to remind Holberg of its wonders.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Mentioned in passing: the Bonewood is noted as ceded to the Thule and excluded from Varushkan settlement.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Mentioned in passing: the Webwood is noted as ceded to the Thule and excluded from Varushkan settlement.

384YE Spring Equinox winds of war.d: The Lasambrian Jotun left Segura, freeing Anduz, then raided Kahraman to secure Gambit. Bregasland stayed quiet as Mathilda Fisher's warband grew. In the Mournwold the Bounders sealed Whittle, admitting only Marchers and angering the magistrates. Eisa Winterborn's Jotun collapsed the western end of Pakaanan's Pass, destroying the Clattering Gulley and the Krampushall, then withdrew into Sermersuaq. There the Empire and Otkodov freed East Floes and pushed the Jotun west. The Druj overran the last Imperial outposts in Ulnak. In Zenith the Empire was about halfway to a beachhead in Clypion, though unliving former Imperials hunted soldiers and the Druj attempted a ritual in Proceris. Four battle opportunities were identified for the summit.

n.Dawn: Dawnish armies had withdrawn from the Forest of Ulnak, and the few outposts they left behind fell silent when the Druj swept back in.
n.Druj: The Druj retook all Imperial-held ground in the Forest of Ulnak. In Zenith they lost ground around Clypion, but they set tormented unliving slaves on the Imperials and began a sinister working in Proceris.
n.Imperial Orcs: The western end of Pakaanan's Pass in their Skarsind homeland was collapsed, and the Clattering Gulley and the Krampushall were destroyed. Movement to Sermersuaq was cut off except through Thule-controlled passes.
n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun abandoned Segura but assaulted Gambit in Kahraman. In the north, Eisa Winterborn's forces completed their mission in Skarsind but were driven west across Sermersuaq.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the summary describes flying past Navarr hearths on the way to Zenith.
n.The Brass Coast: Segura was fully freed when the Jotun withdrew and Anduz was liberated, but Kahraman then came under Jotun assault aimed at Gambit and the town of Rojota.
n.The Marches: Bregasland had a quiet season as Mathilda Fisher's warband grew. In the Mournwold the Bounders sealed Whittle to all but Marchers, angering the magistrates pursuing the heretics there.
n.Thule: The orcs of Otkodov fought alongside the Empire to free East Floes, but they gave no sign that Imperial troops could move freely through their northern passes.
n.Urizen: Imperial armies, including the Citadel Guard with an ensnaring Autumn working, advanced toward a beachhead in Clypion as the fight for Zenith turned in the Empire's favour.
n.Varushka: Varushkan armies had withdrawn from the Forest of Ulnak, leaving outposts that were overrun by the Druj.
n.Wintermark: Imperial armies and their Thule allies freed East Floes and pushed the Jotun west across the Suaq homeland. The pass between Hahnmark and Skarsind remained open.

t.Bregasland: Both the Jotun and the Imperial armies stayed on the defensive and no territory changed hands, while disgruntled Bregas quietly swelled Mathilda Fisher's warband.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the summary refers to the twisted madness at the heart of Brocéliande on the way south to Zenith.
t.Forest of Ulnak: A major Druj force from the south overran the remaining Imperial outposts, and there is no longer any Imperial presence in the forest.
t.Hahnmark: The pass between Hahnmark and Skarsind remained open despite the extensive destruction in Pakaanan's Pass.
t.Kahraman: The Lasambrian Jotun launched an assault focused on Gambit, and a battle opportunity was offered to intercept a Yegarra force moving on the town of Rojota.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the summary passes between Morrow's peaks on its way to Zenith.
t.Mournwold: The Bounders formed a ring of steel around Whittle, letting no one leave and admitting only Marcher magistrates and militia, which angered the magistrates pursuing the sect of Hatred.
t.Otkodov: The orcs of Otkodov fought with the Empire in Sermersuaq but made no indication that Imperial troops could move freely through their passes.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: ghulai from the Sarangrave's swamps were aiding the Druj ritual in Proceris.
t.Segura: The Jotun withdrew entirely, allowing Imperial armies to liberate Anduz and remove all trace of the invaders.
t.Sermersuaq: The Empire and Otkodov freed East Floes and drove the Jotun west, and a battle opportunity was offered to destroy a Jotun fortification with Thule ritual magic.
t.Skarsind: The Jotun collapsed the western end of Pakaanan's Pass, destroying the Clattering Gulley and the Krampushall and cutting the direct route to East Floes.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the Tusks were billeted in Upwold.
t.Zenith: The campaign turned in the Empire's favour, but unliving former Imperials and the miasma complicated the liberation. Two battle opportunities targeted miasma pillars and a Druj ritual.

r.Kahraman/Gambit: The Jotun focused their assault on securing Gambit, and the Empire was offered a chance to stop a Yegarra force bound for Rojota.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: Imperial and Otkodov forces freed East Floes, though the collapsed pass now blocks direct movement to Skarsind.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Movement between the Silver Peaks and Crow's Ridge depends on the Thule, who gave no indication that Imperial troops could pass freely.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: With the pass blocked, the only route from Skarsind to Sermersuaq ran through Thule-controlled passes such as that between Crow's Ridge and the Silver Peaks.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Eisa Winterborn's Jotun collapsed the western end of the pass and destroyed the Clattering Gulley and the Krampushall, blocking movement to East Floes until it is cleared.
r.Zenith/Clypion: Imperial armies were roughly halfway to a beachhead, and the Citadel Guard's ensnaring Autumn magic restricted the Druj armies there.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The Druj were attempting a terrible magical working in the ruined marshes with ghulai aid, and a battle opportunity was offered to intercept the ghulai supplying the Tainted Basilisk ritualists.

A place on a map.d: Gerard La Salle chose the frugal Escovitch for the appraisal. He proposed a fortification at Willstone guarding the Crow Road (70 wains of white granite, 140 crowns, one year, upkeep cut to 5 thrones). In Morrow he proposed four citadels at the Three Watchers (140 wains, 280 crowns, two years, or one with a Synod mandate). In Spiral, Fort Mezudan could be rebuilt (60 wains, 130 crowns, three seasons) if Ateri were Imperial. For Zenith, old records suggest help from Meraud or the tulpa Phellem, or permanent magical citadels with eternal approval. Escovitch then retired, and Lutomysla Niegoslava replaced him.

n.Druj: The Druj hold Zenith and recently attacked Morrow. The proposed Morrow citadels would exploit their evident fear of the Three Watchers, and any Zenith fortification options depend on wresting regions back from them.
n.Grendel: The Grendel's Crow Road from Cinion is identified as an undefended invasion route into Redoubt. Their control of Spiral bars any building there unless Ateri is retaken or Salt Lord Kaliact can be persuaded to cede a rebuilt Fort Mezudan.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: securing Therunin is named alongside liberating Zenith as necessary to end the Druj threat to Morrow.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule's permanent Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae, conjured in the Silver Peaks in 379YE, is cited as a precedent for magically created fortifications in Zenith.
n.Urizen: Urizen received a costed plan for fortifying each of its territories, from Willstone and the Three Watchers to Fort Mezudan. One option calls on the Urizen Assembly to uphold a mandate sending liao to speed garrisoning of the Morrow citadels.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Varushkan Mladen Escovitch wrote the appraisal before retiring to Miekarova, and his successor Lutomysla Niegoslava is a cabalist from Karov.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is not named, though the Silver Peaks in Sermersuaq are cited as the site of an earlier permanent Frozen Citadel.

t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Escovitch's replacement, Lutomysla Niegoslava, is a cabalist from Karov.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Escovitch is retiring to spend his remaining years with his family in Miekarova.
t.Morrow: Morrow, unfortified and recently attacked by the Druj, could gain four citadels around the Three Watchers forming a fortification of strength six thousand. Other options include fortified sword scholar temples and perhaps codifying Phaleron's crystal-sheathing ritual used at Canterspire.
t.Redoubt: Already guarded by the Walls of Cargo and the Court of the White Fountain, Redoubt could close its undefended Crow Road with a new fortification at Willstone. The eternal Adamant has also offered to strengthen the Court of the White Fountain.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the permanent Frozen Citadel conjured by the Thule in the Silver Peaks is cited as a precedent.
t.Spiral: Ceded to the Grendel by treaty, Spiral cannot host Imperial construction. Fort Mezudan could be rebuilt cheaply if Ateri were retaken or Salt Lord Kaliact agreed to cede it.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: securing Therunin is named as necessary, with liberating Zenith, before the Druj threat to Morrow ends.
t.Zenith: Too dangerous to survey, Zenith was assessed from old records instead. Options include Meraud's century-old offer of Summer basalt in return for a thousand pieces of tempest jade, and help from the tulpa Phellem. Permanent magical citadels conjured with an eternal's approval are another possibility.

r.Redoubt/Optarion: Mentioned in passing: Optarion lies at the Redoubt end of the Onyx Path to Ateri, which a rebuilt Fort Mezudan would help defend.
r.Redoubt/Willstone: Willstone's existing citadel could be expanded to guard the Crow Road. The fortification would deter orc bandits troubling visitors to the Grand Conservatory of Music, and charging merchants to store wagons in its courtyard would halve its upkeep.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: a permanent Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae was conjured here by the Thule in Winter 379YE, costing an estimated 240 rings of ilium.
r.Spiral/Ateri: The ruined Fort Mezudan in Ateri could be rebuilt in three seasons for 60 wains and 130 crowns if the Empire controlled the region. While the Onyx Path and the Court of the White Fountain stayed Imperial, the fort would qualify for automatic repair.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Mentioned in passing: Cinion is the Spiral end of the undefended Crow Road, by which Grendel armies could strike at Willstone.
r.Zenith/Clypion: Clypion is named as suitable for a permanent Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae, created instantly once the region was held, given ilium and the eternal's consent.
r.Zenith/Lustri: An ancient record tells of the tulpa Phellem in Lustri's forests offering to help "secure" them; finding it would need a scouting army and then negotiating magicians. A permanent Wooden Fastness is also feasible, though which eternal to approach is unknown.
r.Zenith/Occursion: Occursion is named as suitable for a permanent Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae if the region were held and the eternal agreed.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Proceris could host a permanent Basalt Citadel if Sorin's approval were secured. A permanent Dripping Echoes of the Fen is also possible, though which eternal to ask is unclear.

All the way.d: The Red Wind Corsairs, Winter Sun and Quiet Step advanced on Anduz to find the Lasambrians gone. They had stripped the area of food and wine, and the Corsairs raided their supply lines, taking wagons and prisoners. Segura is wholly Freeborn again. The Hierro, Corazón and Escuta, newly intensified by the relics, entered Gambit with Steven of Sarcombe's Yegarra and offered locals loyalty or exile. Corazón raids threatened white granite and mithril caravans, and the Fort Braydon garrison slowed their advance. A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered a chance to stop the Yegarra-led push on Rojota, and the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills was asked to recover goods looted from Redhill Pastures.

n.Jotun: The Lasambrian families quit Segura with their recovered relics, largely without support from other Jotun, then invaded Kahraman more driven and daring than before, vowing one day to reclaim the Brass Coast.
n.Navarr: The Quiet Step joined the campaign to liberate Segura under Brennos Brackensong, while the Black Thorns marched north to Miaren.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn regained all of Segura and saw Anduz celebrate its liberation, but now face a Lasambrian invasion of Kahraman that threatens Gambit, its people and its precious mining caravans.
n.The Marches: Humans of the Mournwold, the Yegarra under Steven of Sarcombe, travelled south through Jotun lands to fight beside the Corazón and led the vanguard against Rojota.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun forces in Bregasland are noted as having been on the defensive.
t.Kahraman: The Lasambrian Jotun invaded through Gambit, raiding caravans from the Damatian Cliffs and Great Mine of Briante; if they stay another season, white granite and mithril supplies will fall.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: a slow trickle of Freeborn exiles from Gambit flowed east through Rojota and down into Madruga.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns marched north to Miaren after the Winter Solstice.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Yegarra who joined the Lasambrian invasion of Kahraman come from the Mournwold.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian Jotun withdrew from Segura across the border into the hills of Reinos.
t.Segura: The Lasambrian occupation ended and the whole territory returned to Freeborn hands, though Anduz and its villages had been stripped of food and wine before the orcs left.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The Fort Braydon garrison rallied and made the long march south-west to engage the invaders, slowing their advance at the cost of exhaustion.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The orcs and Yegarra overran western Gambit, offering loyalty or exile and looting Redhill Pastures, and threatened Rojota, whose fall would give them a beachhead; a conjunction offered a chance to intercept them.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Corazón raids targeted the mithril caravans from the Great Mine of Briante, and losing Rojota would make such raids considerably easier.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: The Jotun bypassed Damata's hills this time, but Corazón raiders struck caravans carrying white granite from the Damatian Cliffs.
r.Segura/Anduzjasse: The Winter Sun advanced across the plains of Anduzjasse to find Anduz's gates open and its people cheering their liberation.

Assign Breadbasket Spring 383YE.d: The Keeper announced that because the Citadel Guard did not need the Bread Basket that season, and no other army was eligible or had asked for its help, its surplus and the prosperity it provides would go to Bregasland to ease its citizens' suffering. The surplus was welcomed by the inhabitants, but it made no material difference there. The Jotun invasion had not caused widespread famine. The Jotun were not destroying farms and instead wanted the Bregas to keep working them, albeit as thralls. The page notes that the Bread Basket could make a real difference only if a famine struck a Marcher territory, and that any such opportunity would be set out in a Wind of Fortune.

n.Jotun: The Jotun invaders were not destroying Bregas farms and wanted the conquered Bregas to keep working them as thralls. As a result, no famine arose for the Bread Basket to relieve.
n.The Marches: The Marchers' sacrifices were formally recognised by the Keeper's allocation. However, the surplus brought only welcome comfort, not material relief, because the occupied lands were not starving.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland received the Bread Basket's surplus to ease its citizens' suffering under the Jotun invasion. Its inhabitants welcomed it, but it changed little because there was no famine there.

Blood makes noise.d: Sellswords, wagon raiders, wardens, Dawnish knights, Navarr scouts and Imperial Orc preachers poured into Ossium. Thanks to Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov's mandate, the effort focused on freed slaves, who established vales in every region except the Thule-held Webwood and Bonewood. Ossium is now firmly Varushkan, and Nearweald lost its under-developed quality. On offer are several opportunities: sharing the Crawling Depths with local boyars; Lise de Lionsgate's proposed Tower of the Manticore; Ketsov or Senate use of the Mir Mozga in Karsk; and a military assault on Isember, whose bandits attacked Kosti. The Menrothat sept offer black lotus for Farweald, and a conjunction could rescue soldiers trapped at Beetle Tree in Ulnak.

n.Dawn: Dawnish knights and yeofolk flocked to Ossium alongside the Hounds of Glory, and Lise de Lionsgate proposed rebuilding the Tower of the Scorpion as the Tower of the Manticore. The Dawnish Assembly may also urge glory-seekers into Ossium and Ulnak, and a few hundred Ossium natives are petitioning to join Dawn.
n.Druj: The Druj lost their former slaves to Varushka's new vales. They have a force waiting at Beetle Tree to trap Imperial survivors fleeing the Forest of Ulnak, and they still hold Menrothat orcs under their yoke.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a Varushkan mandate would penalise units taking part in the land-based evacuation of Grendel-held Feroz.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: several Highborn are listed among those who ventured into the unknown or went wagon raiding in Ossium.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc preachers led by Bloodcrow Udoo drew more Ossium orcs to Skarsind and made contact with the Menrothat. The sept offers them a dose of black lotus, and knowledge of its use, if the Empire cedes Farweald.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a Varushkan mandate would make Varushka opt out of the raid on Jotun-held Skallahn described in another wind.
n.Navarr: Navarr scouts sent by Nathair Autumngale's mandate helped the settlement, escorted orcs to Skarsind and helped Ossium natives who wished to join the Great Dance.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: a couple of Brass Coast characters are listed among those who aided Ossium.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: several League characters are listed among those who supported the settlement, ventured into the unknown, or went wagon raiding in Ossium.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: a handful of Marchers are listed among those who aided Ossium.
n.Thule: A disciplined Thule force was claiming the land the Senate had ceded to them in Ossium, and no new Varushkan vales were founded in the Thule-dominated Webwood and Bonewood. The Ketsov are courting Thule merchants, and Isember's bandits trade with Thule-held Oloy.
n.Varushka: Varushka gained many new, fervently orthodox citizens and vales across Ossium. It now faces choices over the distrusted Ketsov and the Mir Mozga, and may pass a Synod mandate rallying Varushkans to destroy the bandit haven of Isember.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: two Wintermark characters are listed among those who aided Ossium.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the evacuation of Feroz is cited as one of the actions a Varushkan mandate would discourage.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Druj forces wait at Beetle Tree to trap Dawnish and Varushkan survivors, whom a conjunction could save; success would allow a half-price spy network here. The forest is also proposed as a hunting ground for glory-seeking knights.
t.Karsk: The bandit haven of Isember threatens Karsk; military units and armies here could assault it. The Senate must also decide whether the Ketsov or local vales should harvest the dragonbone of the Mir Mozga.
t.Ossium: Ossium is now firmly Varushkan, with new vales founded by former Druj slaves and settlers, and Nearweald has lost its under-developed quality. Opportunities over the Crawling Depths and the Tower of the Scorpion await the Senate.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Otkodov invaded Karsk in 368YE, helped by some of Isember's inhabitants.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos appears only in the names of League characters listed as supporting Ossium.
t.Semmerholm: Some of the few hundred Ossium natives who chose Dawn over Varushka seek new lives here as yeofolk.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: a Varushkan mandate on Isember would make Varushka opt out of a raid on Skallahn.
t.Skarsind: More orcs left Ossium for Skarsind, often with Navarr escorts along the Varushkan roads.
t.The Barrens: Menrothat orcs live in the northern Barrens under Druj rule, and the sept asks the Empire to cede the Barrens region of Farweald to them.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish knights crossed the Semmerlak on their way to Ossium, many stopping to visit the Golden Causeway.
t.Weirwater: Ossium natives who petitioned to join Dawn seek to start new lives here as yeofolk.

r.Karsk/Kopevnost: Bandits from Isember raided the town of Kosti, but its walls and some vigilant local children foiled them. Kosti's wise ones, led by Valya Sofyn Kosteva, are now calling for Isember's destruction.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Mentioned in passing: Isember's boyar is said to trade with the town of Oloy in Thule-controlled Krevsaty.
r.Karsk/Lestasny: The ruins of Isember, ruled by the outlaw boyar Alexi Iskandrova Isembrioch, are the target of a proposed assault. The untamed Mir Mozga nearby is sought by the Ketsov for a new vale.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: Miners from Moresvah help work the Crawling Depths in Ossium, and Moresvah families would assist if the mine were shared with Ossium's boyars.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Bittershore remains under-developed and gained new vales; some of its former residents chose to petition Dawn instead.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The Bonewood remains Thule-dominated with no new Varushkan vales, though the Ketsov have begun forestry south of it.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Konstantin's outpost near Marshstand Skerry shelters natives wary of the settler-boyars, and Menrothat orcs live in the east. Sharing the Crawling Depths would remove the region's under-populated quality.
r.Ossium/Echofell: The Tower of the Scorpion stands here, and rebuilding it as the Tower of the Manticore would remove the region's under threat quality. The Menrothat also tend the Bone Hives here.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: The Galath Fields remain under-developed, and some former residents sought to join Dawn. A crushing success against Isember, or the Crawling Depths arrangement, could remove a negative quality here.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: Nearweald lost its under-developed quality thanks to the settlement effort and is home to Menrothat settlements.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Webwood remains Thule-dominated, with no new Varushkan vales founded there.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: The Menrothat ask the Empire to cede Farweald to them in exchange for a dose of black lotus and knowledge of its use, provided it will not simply fall back to the Druj.

By fountains, by fishes.d: Bregasland and Odd's End fishing boats and Westerhal's fishing fleet would smuggle Imperial warriors across the Gullet, and any Imperial fleet could also help. Navarr guides would lead the raiders back through Jotun-held Sermersuaq. Hitting forges such as the Steelweaver's Crucible would stop Jotun armies being raised or resupplied. Attacking Kierheim would halt Jotun fortification work. Striking kirkja and Ulfrskelf would recall Jotun orc champions. Raiders could win metals, natural materials and possibly Bourse resources. If more than 20,000 strength took part, every Imperial military unit would suffer a penalty. National assemblies could opt out by mandate. Three Sentinel Gate conjunctions offered ways to strengthen the raid, ease the return or protect the Skallahn spy network.

n.Dawn: Tobias Field proposed a Dawn Assembly mandate urging Dawnish captains to stay out of the Skallahn raid and turn instead to conquering the Barrens. This would spare Dawn the raid's penalty at the cost of weaker Dawnish participation.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are cited as far easier to raid than the Jotun, and a proposed Dawn mandate calls for death to the Druj.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named as easier raiding targets than the Jotun, and alternative mandates propose rescuing people escaping Grendel-held Feroz.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Dawn mandate speaks of standing with Highguard against the Druj, and the Highborn unconquered are compared to Navarr guides.
n.Jotun: The Jotun faced an Imperial raid on Skallahn that could cripple their army resupply, halt their fortification work or force their orc champions home to guard their temples. A Jotun warband near Starkmarsh threatened to expose the Empire's spying, which would put every jarl on alert.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Assembly pledged scouts and pathfinders to lead the raiders out of Skallahn through Jotun-held Sermersuaq. Nathair Autumngale also proposed an alternative mandate steering Navarr captains towards rescuing people fleeing Feroz instead.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Kierheim is described as almost as famous as the League cities of Sarvos and Tassato.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Assembly led the raid and urged Bregasland fisherfolk to lend their boats. It had to choose the raid's targets by statement of principle, and Marcher fleets could join without the penalty other nations' fleets faced.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are named as far easier to raid than the Jotun.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: a special alternative mandate was available to the Varushkan Assembly to focus the nation on the Ossium problem instead of the raid.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark Assembly urged Winterfolk to aid the raid, and Westerhal pledged its fishing fleet to smuggle warriors into Skallahn. Wintermark fleets could join without penalty, and hylje kin could ease the raiders' return.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Freeborn and other Bay of Catazar nations' fleets are noted as being far from the Gullet.
t.Bregasland: Bregasland's fisherfolk and eel farmers were called on to lend boats for the raid. Jotun warriors had been seen coming ashore on the salt flats at Bregasland's edge.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: proposed Brass Coast and Navarr mandates would redirect captains towards liberating or rescuing people held in or escaping Feroz.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: an earlier Marcher judgement spoke of raiding Hordalant, and the Hordalant spy network's loss is cited as a warning.
t.Kallavesa: Two conjunctions led to Kallavesa's Gullet shore, where boats and supplies were being readied for the raid. At Starkmarsh a Jotun warband threatened to expose the Skallahn spy network.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: if the Starkmarsh warband escaped, spying in Jotun territory, including Liathaven, would become twice as hard for a year.
t.Mitwold: The Odd's End fishing fleet would carry raiders, and at Steward's Landing near Odd's End Jarvey Oddsboy sought help to drive off Jotun raiders and hide his preparations. Success would let him send up to 1,500 strength on the raid.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: a special mandate let the Varushkan Assembly focus on the Ossium problem instead of the raid.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Kierheim is compared in fame to Sarvos.
t.Sermersuaq: The raiders' route home ran through Jotun-held western Sermersuaq, where most Imperial losses were expected. Retaking border regions there would reduce the raid's penalty on Imperial forces.
t.Skallahn: Skallahn was the raid's target: a rich territory and seat of Jarl Ustigar of Kierheim. Its forges, its wealth and its sacred kirkja, including Ulfrskelf, were all potential targets, with metals and Bourse resources to be looted.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Kierheim is compared in fame to Tassato.

r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: At Starkmarsh on West Marsh's northern coast, Navarr scouts warned of a Jotun warband that had to be wiped out to keep the Skallahn spy network secret.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: Steward's Landing near Odd's End was a staging post where small boats were being readied for the raid. Jotun raiders threatened it, and Jarvey Oddsboy asked for warriors and a Vale of Shadows ritual to hide it.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: If the Empire took Stark by the end of the season, the penalty on Imperial military units from the raid would fall by one rank.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Taking the Suaq Wastes by the end of the season would ease the raiders' return and cut the raid's penalty by one rank.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: At the Lansipari Pines, hylje threatened by a Kirkland unit would help returning raiders if the orcs were driven off. Taking Tanikipari by season's end would also cut the raid's penalty by one rank.

Carnival of rust.d: Under the Druj miasma and their Rivers of Life curse, the Empire fought slow, grinding engagements in Clypion against the White Lion, Hidden Snake and Red Lizard. The Highborn crusade drove the orcs back, at a cost of about 1,500 Imperial casualties. Unliving Urizen sentinels made by Karvor Eyepeel left Zenith Terrorised, so weakened Imperial armies there now disband. The Citadel Guard's Glass Labyrinth hampers the Druj armies' ability to leave. Two battle opportunities were offered. One was to destroy the Bulwark of Lutum miasma pillars with help from Zakalwe's myrmidons and free key tormented souls. The other was to intercept a caravan from the Palace of the Sleepers bound for the Tainted Basilisk's working in Proceris. Two further conjunctions targeted tormented souls.

n.Dawn: The Eastern Sky made a magically hastened forced march from Holberg to join the Zenith campaign. Its general, Vincent Vexille, pledged to aid Urizen.
n.Druj: The Druj lost about half of Clypion to the Imperial advance and their armies in Zenith are snared by the Glass Labyrinth. They have unleashed tormented sentinels, and the Tainted Basilisk is preparing to poison Proceris.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave and Valiant Pegasus led a costly virtuous crusade that broke the Druj in Clypion. They are the only armies with enough priests to exorcise the tormented souls, and some of those souls are former Highborn.
n.The League: The Wolves of War, bolstered by warbands and heavily armoured free companies from Holberg and Temeschwar, led a grinding advance into Zenith.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard's Autumn magic crippled Druj command in Zenith. However, the Druj have turned fallen Urizen sentinels, sword scholars, warrior-wizards and the seer Yoland into tormented souls that are hostile to their own people.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky marched through Astolat on its way to Zenith.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky marched through Bastion en route to Zenith.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks and Northern Eagle withdrew to Casinea to recover from their wounds, and the Eastern Sky marched through it.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky came fresh from rooting out the Druj in Holberg's marshes, free companies from Holberg joined the Wolves of War, and the Druj once poisoned its forests.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky marched through Morrow, and the Druj could not force the Empire back into Morrow this time.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: two years earlier the Highborn armies were forced back out of Iteri into Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: similar tormented abominations were fought and some freed during the liberation of Reikos, where Isaa and Bakah were once torn apart.
t.Sarangrave: A caravan of Druj warriors and ghulai from the Palace of the Sleepers was heading to Proceris. It carried components that represent more than a year of work in the caverns beneath the palace.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky marched through Semmerholm on its way to Zenith.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: free companies from Temeschwar were recruited to fight with the Wolves of War.
t.Zenith: Zenith saw a seven-army Imperial invasion and the conquest of about half of Clypion. It is now Terrorised by tormented souls, still under the miasma and Rivers of Life, and its Druj armies are trapped by the Glass Labyrinth.

r.Bastion/The Elms: Mentioned in passing: the fallen exarch Benedictian of the Children of the Elms, a Sybella-based chapter, is enslaved as a tormented soul, and the chapter has pledged support if he is laid to rest.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Mentioned in passing: its forests were once poisoned by a Druj poison beast, a precedent for the planned taint of Proceris.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Mentioned in passing: its forests were once poisoned by a Druj poison beast, a precedent for the planned taint of Proceris.
r.Zenith/Clypion: The Empire conquered roughly half of Clypion and is close to a beachhead. A battle opportunity was offered to destroy the Bulwark of Lutum miasma pillars, and the seer Yoland is held at Eridemia's Isolation.
r.Zenith/Iteri: An Imperial beachhead in Clypion would cut Iteri off. Destroying the Clypion pillars would also collapse the miasma over Iteri for at least a year.
r.Zenith/Lustri: Lustri remains a magically defended Druj stronghold with shadows and many-legged guardians, and the Tainted Basilisk gathered resources there. The Sarangrave caravan travels through its woods.
r.Zenith/Occursion: The Tainted Basilisk harvested arcane resources in Occursion, and its miasma will endure for now. It can only be reached through Proceris or from outside Zenith.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Proceris is the heart of Druj power, where the Tainted Basilisk plans to permanently poison the marshes and strengthen its wards. A conjunction to the Fields of Resplendent Twilight offered a chance to intercept the caravan.

Construct Churnspire.d: Proposed by Bastion's senator and seconded by Morrow's, the motion passed at 100 thrones and followed an opportunity described in The Net of the Realms wind of fortune. The tower, designed by Megaris of Glowspire to stand taller than Pakaanan's Pass, required 20 wains of white granite, 10 wains of mithril, 60 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Baal provided the mithril, granite and 7 thrones 4 crowns. The proposed Churnspire Adjutor would receive regalia and a regular gift of mana from Meraud. On scrutiny, the Constitutional Court ruled the title could not be filled by a vote of all Urizen magi. It asked for an administrative motion making it a national title appointed by the Senate.

n.Urizen: Urizen gains a new national title, the Churnspire Adjutor, which carries Meraud's regalia and mana. The Court ruled that the Senate, not a vote of Urizen's magi, must appoint it.

t.Morrow: Morrow is the site of the Churnspire, and its senator seconded the motion to build the tower.

r.Morrow/Peregro: Peregro is where the Churnspire is to be raised, a tower designed to stand taller than Pakaanan's Pass and then be ceded to Meraud.

Construct Great Harbour of Elos.d: Proposed by Volodmartz and seconded by Sarvos, the motion disbursed funds for the Great Harbour of Elos, an opportunity set out in the To see what you sell Wind of Fortune. The harbour was described as a great work yielding prosperous returns to the territory and the tax budget. Construction required 35 wains of weirwood, 35 wains of white granite, 140 crowns in labour and six months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Radomir Ivanovic Volkov provided 5 wains of weirwood and 35 of white granite, and Gancio di Catazar gave 17 thrones 4 crowns and 30 wains of weirwood. On completion, the Elosian Architect, appointed by Imperial Bourse auction with the right to purchase foreign herbs, would become available.

n.Urizen: The restored harbour at Elos promised prosperous returns for Urizen's territory of Redoubt, with the materials and labour largely supplied by citizens of other nations.

t.Redoubt: Redoubt was to gain the restored Great Harbour of Elos, a great work meant to bring prosperity to the territory and the Imperial tax budget once its six-month construction was complete.

r.Redoubt/Naris: Elos in Naris was the site of the Great Harbour, whose restoration required weirwood, white granite and labour and would create the Elosian Architect title on completion.

Construct Grendel Embassy.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Redoubt and seconded by Kahraman, amended the title of Imperial Fleetmaster by commissioning an embassy to the Grendel in Cargo. It passed at no cost in thrones. The Senate chose a standard embassy rather than the large one outlined in the Everything has a price wind of fortune. The embassy required 25 wains of weirwood, 25 wains of white granite, 100 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Summer Solstice 384YE, Sejanus of the Scarlet Guard provided 10 thrones and all the weirwood and white granite, and Ehud gave 2 thrones 4 crowns. Once completed, the Imperial Fleetmaster gains the standard benefits of an embassy.

n.Grendel: The Empire committed to a formal embassy to the Grendel at Cargo, giving the Imperial Fleetmaster a standing diplomatic presence with them, though not the grander embassy the Grendel's offer had proposed.
n.Urizen: Urizen's senator for Redoubt proposed the motion, and the new embassy was to be built at Cargo within Urizen's territory.

t.Redoubt: An Imperial embassy to the Grendel was commissioned at Cargo in Redoubt, with its materials and much of its labour cost provided after the Summer Solstice.

Construct Hufi's Garden.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by Kallavesa. It followed a unanimous greater majority judgement of the Wintermark National Assembly in Autumn 383YE and took up the opportunity described in the All lift together wind of fortune. The garden cost 16 wains of white granite and 32 crowns and would take three months to build. It produces true vervain, bladeroot, imperial roseweald, marrowort and realmsroot. The Woundbinder of the Mark is to inspire Wintermark's grimnir and healers and see that wounded heroes are well tended. The title is to be appointed unanimously by the Wintermark senators, guided by the healers' wishes. Hengest Dun supplied the granite and 4 thrones after the Spring Equinox.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a herb garden and a new national title, the Woundbinder of the Mark, created at the request of its healers and herbalists. The Wintermark senators are to appoint the holder unanimously, and herbalists have pledged up to 67 additional herbs to help save the lives of wounded heroes.

t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's senator seconded the motion, and the garden is to be built in the territory outside Masi.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: Hufi's Garden is to be constructed in Kallavesa Marsh outside Masi, taking three months to complete, and will grow medicinal herbs for the Woundbinder of the Mark.

Construct Pelican Tower.d: Announced under an Imperial Wayleave by Achille di Sarvos, the commission was self-funded at standard sinecure costs. The Pelican Tower will carry a title, the Custodian of the Pelican Tower, held with tenure until death, resignation or reallocation, and appointed by the Senators of the League. After the Spring Equinox 384YE, Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided 10 wains of mithril and 2 thrones 4 crowns towards the work. Once construction is completed, the Custodian of the Pelican Tower may be appointed. The page is a placeholder still being worked on.

n.The League: The League's Senators will appoint the Custodian of the Pelican Tower, a new tenured title, once the tower is complete. The commission was announced by Achille di Sarvos and funded with materials from Giacomo Corvinoscuro.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos is to gain a new sinecure, the Pelican Tower. Its construction was commissioned and supplied with mithril and money after the Spring Equinox 384YE.

r.Sarvos/Foracci: Foracci is the site of the Pelican Tower, and its custodian will be appointed once the building work is finished.

Construct Sanctuary for Justicars.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Kahraman and seconded by the senator for Bastion. The sanctuary was to cost 15 wains of white granite and 30 crowns in labour, with the crowns to be provided by the High Exorcist, and would take three months to build. Once complete it would allow the appointment of a new title, the Justicar of Osseini, serving as a ministry for exorcism. After the Spring Equinox, Delara of the House of the Wanderer provided 3 thrones 5 crowns and the full 15 wains of white granite, and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov provided 1 crown. The page does not record the sanctuary as completed.

n.Grendel: The sanctuary was to be built on the Isle of the Osseini in Grendel-held Feroz, which would place a new Imperial ministry for exorcism, the Justicar of Osseini, on Grendel's island.

t.Feroz: The Isle of the Osseini in Feroz was chosen as the site of the justicars' sanctuary, which would take three months to build and would create the title Justicar of Osseini once finished.

Construct Twilight Demesne.d: Palerictus Ka'bal, the Legion Engineer, commissioned a mana sinecure in Skarsind at the standard cost for sinecures. After the Spring Equinox 384YE several donors supplied materials. Bloodcrow Yargol gave 5 wains of mithril and 2 thrones 4 crowns. Ashborn Vana, Ghillihg, Zerk, Ringforge Kerath and Tog each gave a single wain of mithril. Once work on the Demesne is complete, the title of Curator of the Twilight Demesne will become available for appointment. The page is marked as a placeholder still being worked on, so it records the commission and its progress rather than a finished construction.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Twilight Demesne is being built in Skarsind, an Imperial Orc territory, and will create a new Curator title to oversee a mana sinecure in Orc lands.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind is the site of the Twilight Demesne, a mana sinecure commissioned in Spring 384YE and supplied with mithril by several donors.

Construct spy network in Spiral.d: The commission arose from the opportunity described in the Wind of Fortune The Net of the Realms and was announced by the Imperial Spymaster. It called for a spy network at the Spire of Oblivion's Edge in Spiral, created with the help of the eternal Sung and ceded to that eternal, with no ongoing cost to the budget. The listed cost was 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns in labour, with three months to construct. After the Spring Equinox, Bernard Dugdale provided the 10 wains of mithril and 2 thrones 4 crowns. Once complete it would create a unique spy network in Spiral. The Constitutional Court's concern meant the matter went back to the Senate. The page is an incomplete placeholder.

n.Grendel: The spy network was to be raised in Grendel-held Spiral, though it would be ceded to the eternal Sung rather than placed under Grendel control.

t.Spiral: Spiral was the site of the commissioned spy network at the Spire of Oblivion's Edge, funded with 10 wains of mithril and due to take three months to build, though the Constitutional Court's concern sent the commission back to the Senate.

Dressed in smoke and fire.d: With the League National Assembly's endorsement, Sarvos became the City of Masks, gaining renown for elegance and couture, and the Hag Queen's doom was lifted. Fires ravaged the rebuilt Caricomare docks; the Mayor of Caricomare lost their income and Senate votes but can now buy valuable goods, and the Constitutional Court made it a national Senate appointment open to non-residents. Perhaps a hundred masks gained strange auras and became sought-after. The Mirrored Maschieri planned a 'Feast of Fools' masquerade for the Summer Solstice. Genia Bourné offered her schema-broker network if the League commissions a Brokers Office folly (30 wains each of white granite, weirwood and mithril, 180 crowns, 5 thrones upkeep), appointed annually by the Bourse; the offer lasts a year.

n.The League: The League triumphed over the Hag Queen's attempt to doom Sarvos and is invited to celebrate with a nationwide masquerade at the Summer Solstice. It also has a year to commission a Brokers Office that would let a Bourse-appointed titleholder buy schemas for mage robes, magical jewellery and ritual foci.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos shed the doom of its shattered mirrors to become the City of Masks, famed for fashion, while fires gutted Caricomare's docks and magical auras settled on around a hundred of its masks. The proposed Brokers Office would have to be built in the city, perhaps on the rebuilt Caricomare dockfront.

Equivocate the past.d: The University's true liao is allocated through the Synod's judgement of rewarding, and the Senate could move all Gatekeeper-assigned liao into the Virtue Fund. The Silver Feathers, a sodality devoted to Ruth, offered 6 doses of liao each season if the Librarian proves she is a recognised exemplar. Lud and Moesia, scholars carrying a report on Ratibor of Temeschwar to Senator Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar, were abducted by a surviving Vyig cell. The Vyig demanded 100 Thrones at the Summer Solstice and offered 25 Thrones for Veikko Bondforger's head. The Loyalty Assembly was also given a chance to make its earlier mandate permanent.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Veikko Bondforger previously used the Loyalty Assembly's power to encourage Urizen cooperation with the Grendel in Spiral.
n.Highguard: The Highborn National Assembly is to appoint the first Lepidean Librarian. Highborn citizens pressed for Ruth of Highguard's recognition, and the Heirs of Lepidus begged Highguard's benefactors to help ransom their kidnapped scholars.
n.The League: The League's Senator for Temeschwar, Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar, faced a Vyig ransom demand of 100 Thrones for the scholars and their report on Ratibor. League citizens were also among the founders of the Silver Feathers.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Moesia scorns Lud's view as sounding Urizen, and Urizen with applicable Loyalties were urged to encourage cooperation with the Grendel in Spiral.
n.Varushka: Anastasiya Volkov's statement in the Varushkan assembly commissioned the Ratibor report, which inadvertently alerted the Vyig to Veikko Bondforger's claim to be Ratibor reborn. Varushkan magistrates are holding back from the Vyig drop box until the scholars are safe.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the runesmiths of Runegrott are invoking Isenbrad's legacy in their plan to give Wintermark a rune forge, which makes him a figure of interest to the scholars.

t.Bastion: The Lepidean University, with its renewed library and the Garden of Atun yielding true liao, was completed in the White City. The Silver Feathers held their first meeting there, which worried local magistrates.
t.Karov: The kidnappers gave a Winged Messenger drop box in Karov as their contact. Varushkan magistrates expect it to yield nothing and will not move against it until the scholars are safe or beyond saving.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Cardinal of Loyalty previously urged Urizen to encourage cooperation with the Grendel in Spiral.
t.Temeschwar: Lud and Moesia vanished soon after entering Temeschwar, and a Vyig ransom note was delivered to Ratibor's Gate. This revealed that at least one Vyig cell survived the 379YE purges.

r.Karov/Skoremujac: The kidnappers demanded that the Senator confirm the ransom by Winged Messenger to Cousin Vincenc at the Salting House in Koly, Skoremujac, which magistrates believe is a temporary drop box watched by a single agent.

Expand College of Warcasting.d: Passed in Spring 384YE, the motion commissioned work on the College of Warcasting in Skarsind at a cost of 12 wains of weirwood, 24 crowns in labour and three months of construction. After the Spring Equinox, Bloodcrow Yargol supplied 3 thrones and 4 wains of weirwood, and Ashborn Vana, Ghillihg, Zerk and Ringforge Kerath each supplied 2 wains. Once complete, the Preceptor gains custody of a ministry provided by the Tamazi orcs. Although the motion's text named the Bourse voting style, the recorded outcome is that the Preceptor is now chosen by Tally of the Votes, cast by Imperial Orc military unit owners who supported an Imperial army in the previous year.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Preceptor of the Warcaster College now answers to Imperial Orc military unit owners who have supported an Imperial army, giving the nation's fighting bands a direct say in the title, while Imperial Orc citizens supplied the weirwood and money for the work.

t.Skarsind: The College of Warcasting in Skarsind is being expanded with a ministry provided by the Tamazi orcs, placed in the custody of its Preceptor once the three months of construction are complete.

Expand Mana Ministries.d: The motion took up the opportunity described in the Honey and Vinegar Wind of Fortune to upgrade the League's mana ministries, which serve the grandmasters of the Conclave orders. It passed at 200 thrones. The listed costs were 60 wains of mithril and 120 crowns in labour, with six months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Oscuro Kira di Tassato gave 2 thrones, and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos and Catellus di Tassato-Regario gave 1 throne each. After the Summer Solstice, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato gave 60 wains of mithril and 11 thrones. Once complete, each grandmaster will have more mana available.

n.The League: The League's three mana ministries were chosen for upgrade. League citizens from Tassato and Sarvos provided the thrones and mithril recorded towards the work.

t.Sarvos: The mana ministry in Sarvos was one of the three to be upgraded, and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos contributed a throne towards the work.
t.Tassato: Tassato's senator proposed the motion and its mana ministry was among those to be upgraded. Citizens styled di Tassato supplied most of the recorded funding and all 60 wains of mithril.
t.Temeschwar: The mana ministry in Temeschwar was one of the three to be upgraded, increasing the mana available to the grandmasters it serves.

Extend Iron Roads.d: Proposed by the senator for Ossium and seconded by Volodmartz, the motion took up the opportunity set out in the Thousands or more wind of fortune. Because Ossium is under-developed, labour costs rose by two-fifths, giving a requirement of 70 wains of white granite and 140 crowns in labour, plus six months of construction beyond the main Iron Roads project. From Autumn 383YE to Winter 384YE, contributions of granite and thrones came from several donors, most of all Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov. Once complete, the roads will function as a great work and remove a negative quality from one of Ossium's regions, depending on the situation at the time.

n.Varushka: Varushkan senators for Ossium and Volodmartz proposed and seconded the extension. Varushkans such as Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov supplied much of the white granite to bring the Iron Roads into their lands.

t.Ossium: Ossium is to receive its own stretch of the Iron Roads, though its under-developed state made the labour dearer. When finished, the roads should lift a negative quality from one of its regions.

False kings.d: The Jotun, aided by fey knights from the Fields of Glory, dug in defensively in North Fens and Grey Fens, and no battle was fought, so control did not change. The Strong Reeds lay low, rearmed from equipment recovered at Miresend, while Night magic in Ottermire set lantern-bearing marsh creatures against the invaders. Steven of Sarcombe's Mournwold Exiles had left, but several hundred newcomers from Hordalant and around 250 former Marcher citizens swelled Mathilda's warband. Her messengers urged secession and offered a Jotun pause on claims to Marcher lands if Bregasland's independence were recognised. A conjunction offered the Empire a chance to defeat a Jotun warband in Grey Fens and discredit her.

n.Jotun: Jotun armies stayed on the defensive in Bregasland, backing Mathilda Fisher under a treaty recognising an independent Bregasland, and offering to set aside their claim to the Mourn, Mitwold and Upwold for five years if Bregasland's independence were recognised.
n.The Marches: The Marches faced a growing secessionist movement in Bregasland, with about 250 former citizens openly joining Mathilda Fisher, and Marcher military units given the treasonous option of fighting alongside the Jotun-backed rebels.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland saw no battles, but it was divided: southern and eastern households loudly professed loyalty while the north and west weighed the future, and Mathilda's recruitment threatened to grow each season.
t.Hordalant: Several hundred people dressed in a mix of Bregas and Jotun fashion crossed out of Hordalant to join Mathilda's warband, and she claims her household has dwelled in Hordalant's marshes for some four hundred years.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold was named among the Marcher lands the Jotun would leave alone for five years if Bregasland's independence were recognised, and Mathilda told the Bregas to leave the Empire to Mitwold's squabbling households.
t.Mournwold: Steven of Sarcombe's Mournwold Exiles, driven by grief over the curses that struck the Mourn, had left Bregasland, and the Mourn was included in the Jotun offer to suspend their claims.
t.Upwold: The Tusks were billeted in comfort in Upwold, and Upwold was among the lands the Jotun offered not to pursue for five years in return for Bregas independence.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: The Jotun still held Grey Fens, though shakily, and a cautious Jotun picket for the Fist of Ulven roamed there; the village of Dank Mere offered to rebut Mathilda's propaganda if the Empire defeated it through the Sentinel Gate.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: The Jotun remained firmly in control of North Fens, building palisades, while their fey allies held tourneys and banquets among the northern marshes; Mathilda claims it as Fisher land.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: Night magic woven into Ottermire made the marshes resist the Jotun, with lantern-bearing creatures luring orc camps into the quagmires, though Mathilda counts Ottermire as Fisher land.

Fixing What is Broken.d: The Marcher Assembly had passed two statements with primacy, by Nicolas Reaper and Sister Meredith, urging threshers to bring sorcerers to Imperial justice and calling cursing treason. Threshers feared risking their lives only for the law to do nothing, since no one was punished for the earlier curses or for Navarr flouting the interdiction. A proposed Marcher Assembly mandate would reassure them, reinvigorating threshers to hunt sorcerers Empire-wide, but would risk apoplectic anger if future curses go unpunished. Alisoun Bathwater instead asked the Vigilance Assembly to endorse threshers dealing with sorcerers by any means necessary, reviving the old tradition of direct action. The two mandates are not in competition and would inspire different groups of threshers.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Alisoun Bathwater jibes that Imperial law works best when instructed by a Dawnishman, and notes the Cardinal of Vigilance she appeals to is Dawnish.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr are cited as having flouted the interdiction on Rivers Run Red without anyone being punished.
n.The Marches: Marcher threshers, unsettled by fears that the curse interdiction might be lifted, could be steered either towards lawful pursuit of sorcerers through a Marcher Assembly mandate or towards direct action through a Vigilance Assembly mandate, both still only proposals.

t.Mournwold: The memory of the Mournwold's devastation by Imperial curses three years earlier is the root of the threshers' anger and the debate over how to deal with sorcerers.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Alisoun Bathwater suggests the Empire's response would have been very different had Rivers Run Red and Mountain Murders the Children been used on Semmerholm.

Given and denied.d: The Summer Storm, Marcher Drakes, Bloodcloaks and Green Shield gathered at Atalaq with nearly fourteen thousand warriors from independent warbands. The Thule laid the Rivers of Life enchantment over Sermersuaq and fell on the Jotun from the north. East Floes was liberated, and the Empire came four-fifths of the way to conquering Suaq Fount before the Jotun made a stand at Ikka's Tears. Each side lost roughly two thousand soldiers. The Jotun collapsed the western end of Pakaanan's Pass, destroying the Clattering Gulley and the Krampushal. The Thule offered to destroy a Jotun fortress if Imperial forces escorted their warlocks to the Pyhatunturi regio. A separate raid on Ikka's Trail could also seize four wains of mithril.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish heroes were among those fighting with the Autumn-enchanted Wintermark army, their bright tabards seen under fur coats.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm fought at the heart of the Imperial push, and the Shield of the Mountain treated the orcs of Skarsind as respected rivals, with some soldiers hearing Sjöfn of the Bittenblade urging glorious conquest or death. The sealing of Pakaanan's Pass cut Skarsind off from Sermersuaq.
n.Jotun: The Jotun lost East Floes and were driven back across Suaq Fount to a stand at the Pride of Ikka's Tears, losing around two thousand warriors. They fulfilled their threat to seal Pakaanan's Pass and swore not to forgive the Thule for siding with the Empire.
