n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr fought within the Wintermark army, and a Navarr messenger brought the Summer Storm word that Pakaanan's Pass had been sealed.
n.Thule: Three Thule armies joined the campaign as allies of the Empire, and their Rivers of Life enchantment greatly reduced the loss of life. Their warlocks offered to annihilate a Jotun fortification with the power of the Five-Who-Are-One, while making plain what such magic could do to others.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks and the Green Shield led the campaign to begin reclaiming Sermersuaq, liberating East Floes and pressing into Suaq Fount. Winterfolk heroes were singled out for challenge by Eisa Winterborn's Yegarra, and Rakner Ravenstorm was asked to lead a raid for mithril.

t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is not named; the page only involves the Thule armies and warlocks who joined the campaign from the north.
t.Sermersuaq: Imperial and Thule armies liberated East Floes and came close to taking Suaq Fount, but the Jotun still hold the mine at Ikka's Tears and their fortresses in Stark and Tanikipari. The territory is no longer linked to Skarsind by Pakaanan's Pass.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the Yegarra under Eisa Winterborn may be descendants of Suaq thralls raised among the Jotun in Tromsa and Skallahn.
t.Skarsind: The Jotun collapsed the western end of Pakaanan's Pass, so armies can no longer pass between Skarsind and Sermersuaq.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: the Yegarra under Eisa Winterborn may be descendants of Suaq thralls raised among the Jotun in Tromsa and Skallahn.

r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: After fierce fighting, including the fall of a Jotun camp at Wreck and the Battle of the Three Armies, East Floes was liberated by the Empire.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: The Imperial armies mustered at Atalaq in Sealtoq, where a Thule warlock camped outside the walls and sent messenger lizard-owls north-east before the advance.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: the retreating Jotun armies kept well clear of the foothills of the Silver Peaks as the Thule struck from the north.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The Fastness of Kalant in Stark was cut off by months of blizzard and failed to support the Jotun. It is now one of the two fortresses the Thule have offered to destroy.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: The Empire is four-fifths of the way to conquering Suaq Fount, but the Jotun hold the Pride of Ikka's Tears. Suaq thralls there have hidden stolen ore that a raid on Ikka's Trail could carry off.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: The Jotun are moving mithril into the Suaq Wastes. The Pyhatunturi regio there, held by Eisa Winterborn's Yegarra and used by the Ice Dragon, is the site of the Thule ritual battle opportunity.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: Olgafsdottirshal in Tanikipari was kept out of the campaign by blizzard and is one of the two fortresses the Thule have offered to destroy.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: The Jotun sealed the western end of the pass, closing the route to Sermersuaq and destroying the Clattering Gulley and the Krampushal.

Improve Court of the White Fountain.d: The improvement was a special opportunity arising from the Stone and Stone wind of fortune, costing 10 rings of ilium and taking three months to complete. Edmundo of Damakhan's Forge agreed to supply the ilium and provided the 10 rings after the Spring Equinox 384YE. Cato Auricspire of the Scarlet Guard was to organise a ritual to be cast on completion. The plans also included an office and suite of rooms for a new Captain of the Fountain's Guard, a tenured national position chosen by the general or generals of Urizen and responsible for the fortress and for the morale and training of its guards. The outcome was not recorded.

n.Urizen: Urizen stood to gain a strengthened fortress and a new tenured national title, the Captain of the Fountain's Guard, appointed by its generals, with Urizen citizens supplying the ilium and organising the completion ritual.

t.Redoubt: The Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt was to be rebuilt over three months to be unbreakable, with an office and rooms added for the captain of its guard.

Improve Towerjacks.d: Proposed by the Senator for Astolat and seconded by the Conscience of the Senate, the motion passed with the full amount disbursed to the Senator for Astolat. The improvement required 50 wains of mithril and 100 crowns. Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg contributed a small sum after the Spring Equinox, and Natalia 'The Falcon' Barossa supplied the remaining mithril and most of the coin across the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox. To complete the work, the Towerjacks' general must order the army back to Holberg for a season before the Spring Equinox 385YE, entering in triumph through the Holmauer Gate and processing through the city, which can be done while the army rests and recuperates.

n.The League: The Towerjacks, bound to Holberg, the city they fought for years to save, were to become engineers rather than siege troops, with Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg among those funding the work.

t.Holberg: Holberg was to host the Towerjacks for a season, as the army must return to the city before Spring 385YE to complete its transformation.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: The Towerjacks were to enter Holberg in triumph through the Holmauer Gate and parade through the streets as part of completing their improvement.

On the outside looking inside.d: The new Consulate raised the Imperial Consul's prestige, and the Senate could now strip the Fleet Master of representing the Empire to the Grendel. The Sumaah Symposium shrank to one injured cardinal, Cosatti, after food poisoning. Asavean hostility grew, and Axou anger over the Tamazi cut trade at the Black Sails Quay, though the Elosian Docks, Kantor enclave and House of Spirits were completed. The Commonwealth built the Lyceum Schloss and offered four rituals to the Conclave. Jarm gave the Senate until Summer to disavow war or lose all ties. A Bregasland delegation sought the Marchers, and a conjunction offered a chance to rescue magistrate Kaisa Kaisasbarn from captors near Kabalai Campo.

n.Dawn: The devout Free Folk exiles have settled at Caer Faucon under the Lady of the Proffered Hand, and some came to Anvil to question Imperial priests about why their Way is considered wrong.
n.Grendel: With the Consulate complete, the Senate could remove the Imperial Fleet Master's role as representative to the Grendel, forcing them to deal with the Imperial Consul; mutual sanctions still hamper trade with Oran.
n.Highguard: Highborn congregation leaders were to appoint the first Bursar of the Axou House of Spirits in Mareholm, while Necropolis saw falling Axou trade at the Black Sails Quay and received the Sumaah list of inspirations at its embassy.
n.Imperial Orcs: Fal of the Imperial Orcs, as Imperial Consul, gained a new Consulate, greater standing and authority over the Bregasland delegation, while Ashborn Pakt faced worsening relations as Ambassador to Asavea.
n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun pulled back from Kahraman into Reinos, and the Bregasland delegation sent by their human ally Mathilda Fisher could technically be seen as representing the Jotun.
n.Navarr: Gelert Ashborn, the Navarr Ambassador to Jarm, faced a Jarmish ultimatum blamed on a lack of Imperial correspondence, and a Navarr striding escorted Cardinal Cosatti to Anvil.
n.The Brass Coast: Magistrates pursued Freeborn and Faraden smugglers in Segura while the National Assembly stayed silent. The Commonwealth built the Lyceum Schloss in Madruga, and the Marracossan exiles in Trajadoz sought formal recognition.
n.The League: Tassato gained the Imperial Consulate but its Jarmish lodge and mana exchange were threatened by the ultimatum, while in Sarvos the Sarcophan enclave prospered and the Cavabianca Docks' Asavean backers came under pressure.
n.The Marches: A delegation from Mathilda Fisher in Bregasland arrived wishing to speak first with Marchers and the Bregas, and Faraden merchants at Moonwater Hall in Upwold obstructed the smuggling inquiry.
n.Thule: The Thule fought alongside Imperial armies in Sermersuaq and claimed Miechernya and Webwood under treaty, raising a query about army numbers and offering a meeting via the Hall of Worlds.
n.Urizen: The Elosian Docks were completed on the Redoubt coast, Urizen's places of learning expected Axou students, and Urizeni Ambassador Tarquinius Ankarien faced public Axou anger.
n.Varushka: Varushka saw Miechernya in Miekarova and Webwood in Ossium pass to Thule control under the treaty, and Varushkan Ambassador Yevgeni Katzev handled continued peace with Otkodov.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark magistrate Kaisa Kaisasbarn was captured while investigating smugglers, prompting a rescue conjunction, and Thanmir Hrafnar serves as Ambassador to the friendly Sarcophan Delves.

t.Astolat: The Asavean Free Folk have moved to Caer Faucon and are settling in easily beside their Dawnish neighbours.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named on the page and is linked only through the maritime trade it describes.
t.Bregasland: After the Yegarra and Jotun were beaten at Miresend, Mathilda Fisher remained at Fisher's Rock and sent a delegation to Anvil to speak with the Bregas.
t.Casinea: The Axou House of Spirits, a campus of the Halls of Maykop, was completed in Mareholm, and the Sumaah delegation fell ill at Casca's Fall.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Grendel control of Feroz is cited as one reason few Suranni merchants trade north.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the University of Holberg is among the institutions expecting Axou students.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the presence of the Lasambrian Jotun in Kahraman slowed the magistrates' smuggling investigation.
t.Madruga: Commonwealth workers built the fortified Lyceum Schloss on the Isle of the Lyceum, improving its ability to codify army enchantments, with scholars due after the Equinox.
t.Miekarova: Thule armies moved in to claim Miechernya, ceded to them under the treaty that secured their aid.
t.Necropolis: Angry Axou traders shunned the Black Sails Quay, worsening its liao deals, while the Sumaah list of inspirations was lodged at the Imperial Embassy there.
t.Ossium: Thule armies moved in to claim Webwood under the terms of the treaty.
t.Otkodov: The Empire remained at peace with the Thule of Otkodov, who proposed talks on the Sermersuaq war in Lashonar's caucus forum.
t.Redoubt: The Axou Elosian Docks were completed on the Redoubt coast, with an associated Imperial title due for appointment.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian Jotun were seen retreating back into Reinos.
t.Sarvos: The new Sarcophan enclave was thriving, while the Asavean families backing the Cavabianca Docks were pressured to stop trading with the Empire.
t.Segura: Magistrates were investigating a smuggling ring here, Suranni traders reported the Arav purge, and magistrate Kaisa Kaisasbarn vanished nearby.
t.Sermersuaq: Three Thule armies fought alongside Imperial armies, and the Thule queried whether the treaty required them always to be outnumbered there.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: listed only in further reading on the Grendel in Spiral.
t.Tassato: The Imperial Consulate was completed here, but the Jarmish lodge and the extra mana at the Tassato Mana Exchange would be lost if Jarm severed ties.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Faraden merchants using the Moonwater Hall enclave were described as uncooperative with the magistrates.

r.Casinea/Casfall: The Sumaah Symposium delegation was struck down with food poisoning while resting at Casca's Fall, leaving only Cardinal Cosatti to continue.
r.Casinea/Mareholm: The Axou House of Spirits was completed near the Silent Sentinel, with its first students expected the following month.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: Thule armies took control of Miechernya, ceded to them by treaty in return for aid in Sermersuaq.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Thule armies took control of Webwood, ceded to them under the treaty.

One side stone, one side fire.d: The koboldi warned that trogoni breeding in the sinkhole would eventually erupt against mines and mana sites in southern Hahnmark, Temeschwar, northern Upwold and Miaren. The Master of the Koboldi could announce the door's installation, opening an Expedition to the Depths for Imperial military units. The more strength committed, the deeper the seal: from the natural caverns, costing the Delver of the Depths income, down to the Terunael Mineworkings, ancient tunnels or trogoni burrows, each bringing greater treasure. If the door was not in place by the Winter Solstice 384YE, a trogoni horde might emerge. Several National Assemblies could urge support, League armies could assist, and the koboldi shared the secret of Red Iron wards.

n.Dawn: The Dawn National Assembly could urge knights to seek glory in the abyss, granting Dawnish units a rank bonus, full access to later exploration and more mithril and ilium for all delvers if the burrows were reached.
n.Navarr: The Navarr National Assembly could urge Navarr to help reach the Terunael Mineworkings, giving their units a rank bonus and, at 5,000 strength, a report for the Advisor on the Vallorn on what their ancestors did there.
n.The League: The Towerjacks or Wolves of War could be sent to a bordering territory to storm the depths, adding half their base strength and boosting League units, at the cost of halved defence and no resupply.
n.The Marches: The Marches National Assembly could urge Marchers to remove the threat to Upwold, earning participating Marcher units 24 rings each from grateful households.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark National Assembly could call on Winterfolk heroes to face the trogoni, granting their units a rank bonus and, if the ancient tunnels were reached, rune secrets for the Runegrott Runeforge.

t.Hahnmark: Southern Hahnmark's mines and mana sites, bolstered by Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance, were thought the likeliest first target should the trogoni horde erupt.
t.Miaren: Northern Miaren, possibly including Seren and the Eternal Flame, lay under threat of a trogoni eruption, and League armies could be sent there to aid the expedition.
t.Temeschwar: Southern Temeschwar's mana sites, including those boosted by Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty, were at risk from the trogoni, and it was one of the territories where League armies could join the expedition.
t.Upwold: Northern Upwold borders the sinkhole and faced a trogoni threat, and its households would pay Marcher units that helped seal the hole if the mandate passed.

r.Miaren/Goldglades: Goldglades was named as directly threatened by the trogoni, one reason given for Navarr to support sealing the sinkhole.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: Part of the Vardstein Vale had fallen into the sinkhole, and the wilderness now faced mana-hungry trogoni drawn to nearby mana sites.
r.Upwold/Birchland: The sinkhole opened in Birchland, swallowing households, and its people would be foremost among those paying Marcher units who helped seal it.

Pebbles drawn from a heap.d: The Urizen National Assembly upheld a mandate by Alcuin, backed by Cardinal Veikko Bondforger. Tarquinius's statement offered a middle way, and Palaphon Ankarien's Conclave declaration warned that sharing magical secrets could be sorcery. Spiral's citizens therefore warded the Salt Lord's palace free, with further wards for payment. The Grendel accepted, and the Citadel Guard stopped deteriorating until after Summer. The Salt Lord proposed a Senate-created Spiral Envoy, and the Northern Mareave Trading Consortium offered to buy weirwood and white granite. The Circle of Black Sand sought to trade ritual lore. Speaker Morna would visit Anvil over the robbery of Maistir Bradach. The opportunities lasted until the end of Autumn 384YE.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the page only refers to the malign forces of the Black Plateau, which the mithril wards guard against.
n.Grendel: Salt Lord Kaliact accepted free wards for her palace and paid for any others, and her merchants, the Northern Mareave Trading Consortium and the Circle of Black Sand sought trade, while Speaker Morna was coming to Anvil to demand answers, and perhaps reparations, for the robbery of Maistir Bradach.
n.Urizen: Urizen kept the Block's secrets while warding the Salt Lord's palace, faced only a modest tribute and regained support for the Citadel Guard. It was also offered a national Spiral Envoy title and a white granite for mithril exchange.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Salt Lord's hands-off rule in Spiral is contrasted with the Grendel approach in Feroz, and an earlier Feroz Wind is listed for further reading.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the Northern Mareave Trading Consortium, which offered to buy weirwood and white granite, takes its name from the region, though its representative was based in Apulian.
t.Redoubt: Grendel merchants began crossing the Onyx Path and Crow Road into Redoubt to trade for Urizen mana and metals, paying border tariffs. The Salt Lord planned to send armed mithril caravans through the Crow Road pass.
t.Spiral: Spiral was now wholly under Grendel rule, but its Urizen resources counted as being in a foreign rather than a conquered territory while the détente lasted. Its people paid a moderate tribute, warded the Salt Lord's palace and could again support the Citadel Guard.

r.Spiral/Apulus: The Salt Lord's palace in Apulian received the Block's mithril wards free, and the city became the hub for Grendel trade with the Consortium's representative and the Circle of Black Sand based there.
r.Spiral/Screed: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel merchant in the opening fiction complained of nightmares and a feeling of insignificance caused by 'the place in Screed'.

Set a twisted thing straight.d: The Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave and Valiant Pegasus launched a virtuous crusade beside the Eastern Sky, Wolves of War, Iron Helms and Citadel Guard. Scores died, but every Highborn felt inspired, and anointed Highborn gain extra heroism while fighting in Zenith. Proposed mandates could swell the Citadel Guard with Urizeni survivors if it stays until Zenith is freed, spur Highborn and Dawnish armies to race for the Barrens, or penalise armies leaving Zenith. Highguard's acceptance of Dawn's challenge opened Dawnish territories to both nations' armies with improved resupply. Unbound Winter spirits animated corpses around Winter regio in Clypion. Two conjunctions, at Lutum Descent and Kyrinian Spring, offered chances to destroy or ward these regio.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish Assembly's challenge was taken up by Highguard, so Dawnish and Highborn armies may pass freely through Dawnish territories to the Barrens with better resupply. A proposed mandate would let Dawnish armies make triumphant charges there next season.
n.Druj: The Druj were forced reluctantly to give ground in Zenith before a seven-army assault. Warding the Kyrinian Spring regio could drive Winter spirits towards their armies, inflicting perhaps 250 casualties.
n.Highguard: All three Highborn armies launched their first virtuous crusade into Zenith, inspiring every Highborn citizen and granting anointed Highborn extra heroism there. Their Assembly also accepted Dawn's Barrens challenge, with a further mandate proposed to commit Highborn forces to the race.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Udoo had declared the Imperial Orcs' ambition to take the Barrens, but the nation did not answer Dawn's challenge and no Imperial Orc armies attacked there.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr is noted as one of the nations bordering the Barrens.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: League forces are listed among the armies in Zenith threatened by the risen dead, and the League is noted as bordering the Barrens.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Citadel Guard fought alongside the Highborn crusade, and a proposed mandate could rally experienced Urizeni survivors and refugees to its banner, at the risk of mass desertion if it leaves Zenith before liberation. Unchecked Winter spirits could turn on Zenith's remaining Urizeni if no Imperial armies stay.
n.Varushka: The Iron Helms fought in Zenith as the Winter spirits once bound to them broke free, and a Varushkan cabal with that army proposed warding the Kyrinian Spring regio with Hold Back Frozen Hunger.

t.Morrow: The three Highborn statues guarding the passes between Morrow and Zenith inspired the crusade, and Urizeni refugees in Morrow might join the Citadel Guard if the Urizen mandate passes.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni refugees who fled to Redoubt are among those who might join the Citadel Guard.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens became the prize in a proposed race between Highguard and Dawn, with the nation taking the most regions holding the rightful claim, though no Imperial army had yet moved against them.
t.Zenith: Seven Imperial armies drove into Zenith against stubborn Druj defenders, while freed Winter spirits raised the dead and threatened both armies and the surviving Urizeni population.

r.Zenith/Clypion: Spontaneous Winter regio erupted across Clypion, sustaining spirits that animated the dead, and missions to the Lutum Descent and Kyrinian Spring were proposed to close or ward them. Failure could cost Imperial armies 250 extra casualties.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Mentioned in passing: the Lutum Descent valley is described as leading down to Iteri as well as into Clypion.

Some kind of fight.d: Nearly thirty Navarr military units, with prognosticator Rhian Swiftlark, scouted Liathaven from its spy network; their leaders carried a report offering a chance to attack the Heirs of Terunael. Several hundred vallornspawn left Vale's Lament for Mareholm, trapping the villagers of Holmwood, while Holberg free companies of the Towerjacks moved to oppose them. Twinned conjunctions offered a choice: save Holmwood and let Shadowspore escape, or strike at Shadowspore at Vale's Fast and leave the villagers to be slaughtered. The General of the Towerjacks was suggested to decide. Separate conjunctions offered chances to hold a spring regio at Broch's Approach and to save Black Hearth Steading in Black Boughs for reoccupation by the Autumn Equinox.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Holberg soldiers are described as hardened by fighting the Druj on their besieged city walls.
n.Highguard: A vallornspawn horde invaded Mareholm in the Highborn territory of Casinea, trapping the farming settlement of Holmwood, whose people could be saved only if the Empire chose that conjunction.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are noted as known enemies controlling the northern regions of Liathaven, where the Navarr scouts operated.
n.Navarr: The Navarr sent nearly thirty units and a team of prognosticators under Rhian Swiftlark into Liathaven to find the Heirs of Terunael, while their thorns tracked the spawn into Mareholm and their former steading of Black Hearth faced destruction by heralds of Yaw'nagrah.
n.The League: Holberg free companies of the Towerjacks moved to fight the spawn in Mareholm, and the General of the Towerjacks was suggested to choose which of the twinned conjunctions the Empire would take.

t.Brocéliande: The spawn horde emerged from Vale's Lament, and conjunctions opened to Broch's Approach, where vallorn were drawn to a spring regio, and to Black Hearth Steading in Black Boughs, both steeped in vallorn miasma.
t.Casinea: Several hundred vallornspawn directed by Shadowspore crossed into Mareholm and surrounded Holmwood, with the Towerjacks resupplying in the region moving to stand against them.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the free companies attached to the Towerjacks come from Holberg, whose city walls are described as besieged by the Druj.
t.Liathaven: Navarr scouts worked from a concealed spy network to trace the Heirs of Terunael to the unconquered vallorn heart, returning with a report and an opportunity to attack them; the Empire held only a handful of steadings here amid Jotun and Feni.

r.Brocéliande/Black Boughs: Heralds of Yaw'nagrah tearing down signs of civilisation threatened ruined Black Hearth Steading; keeping them from its palisade for ten minutes would allow it to be reoccupied by the Autumn Equinox, while failure would see it destroyed.
r.Brocéliande/Vale's Lament: A host of vallornspawn shambled out of Vale's Lament across the border into Mareholm, though the vallorn's miasma did not spread with it.
r.Casinea/Mareholm: The spawn horde corralled the villagers of Holmwood in its farm buildings and chapel; choosing the Holmwood conjunction would save everyone but leave the settlement badly damaged, while choosing Vale's Fast would see them slaughtered.

Some kind of trouble.d: Four major conjunctions were listed. Two on Saturday would channel Thule ritual magic to destroy a fortification at Pyhatunturi in Sermersuaq, perhaps reducing Cathan Canae's aid to the Jotun, and intercept a Lasambrian Jotun and Yegarra force seeking to take Rojota and a beachhead in Gambit. Two on Sunday targeted the Druj in Zenith: destroying miasma pillars with Zakalwe's aid and intercepting ghulai supplying the Tainted Basilisk ritualists. Fifteen large conjunctions covered exorcisms, raids, the Skallahn spy network, the vallorn in Brocéliande and Casinea, and winter regio work. Three small conjunctions involved rescues and selecting heroes for the Summer Tourney.

n.Dawn: In Dawn's Semmerholm, Hayaak chose five people to organise teams at the Forest of Affray to select heroes for the Summer Tourney.
n.Druj: The Druj were the enemy at both Sunday major conjunctions in Zenith, where Imperial forces aimed to destroy their miasma pillars and intercept ghulai supplying the Tainted Basilisk ritualists. A further opportunity in the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak sought to enable the return of Imperial soldiers.
n.Grendel: The Hand of Guerra had an opportunity to rescue several Zemress Islanders in the Afar Hills of Grendel-held Feroz.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Casinea faced the vallorn, with the General of the Towerjacks deciding how to combat it in Mareholm. A fallen Highguard Exarch was also to be exorcised in Zenith.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were the main foe: Yegarra-aided forces in Sermersuaq faced Thule ritual magic against a fortification, Lasambrian raiders threatened Kahraman, and a Jotun warband was to be defeated in Bregasland. Imperial preparations for a raid on Jotun-held Skallahn were also under way.
n.The Brass Coast: Kahraman was threatened by a Lasambrian Jotun and Yegarra push on Rojota and Gambit, which the Empire sought to intercept. In Segura, missions were planned to rescue a lost magistrate and magicians taken by the Iron Confederacy.
n.The Marches: The Senator for Bregasland was to lead an attack on a Jotun warband in the Grey Fens to counter Mathilda Fisher's propaganda. In Mitwold, the Shuttered Lantern was to hide preparations for the Skallahn raid.
n.Thule: Thule ritual magic was to be channelled by Imperial forces to destroy a Jotun fortification at Pyhatunturi in Sermersuaq.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Sermersuaq saw a major battle against the Jotun and Yegarra, a raid on a mithril mine and an effort to enlist the Hylje. Kallavesa's West Marsh hosted work to keep the Skallahn spy network secret.

t.Bregasland: A Jotun warband at Dank Mere was to be defeated, under the Senator for Bregasland, to combat Mathilda Fisher's propaganda.
t.Brocéliande: Imperial forces aimed to disperse vallornspawn near a regio at Broch's Approach and to defend a steading at the Black Hearth Wayhouse.
t.Casinea: The General of the Towerjacks was to decide how to combat the vallorn at Holmwood or Vale's Fast in Mareholm.
t.Feroz: The Hand of Guerra had a small conjunction to rescue several Zemress Islanders in the Afar Hills.
t.Forest of Ulnak: The Imperial Spymaster had a conjunction at the Beetle Tree in Oerwealt to enable the return of Imperial soldiers.
t.Kahraman: A Lasambrian Jotun and Yegarra force threatened to take Rojota and secure a beachhead in Gambit, and Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills was to make an example of Lasambrian raiders at Redhill Pastures.
t.Kalino: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Confederacy, which held Kalino, had taken magicians whom the Celestial Arch sought to rescue from Kalino Watch in Segura.
t.Kallavesa: The Imperial Spymaster was to maintain the secrecy of the Skallahn spy network at Starkmarsh in the West Marsh.
t.Mitwold: The Grandmaster of the Shuttered Lantern was to hide preparations for the Skallahn raid at Steward's Landing in Oddmire.
t.Segura: A magistrate lost investigating smugglers was to be rescued at Kabalai Campo, and magicians were to be rescued from the Iron Confederacy at Kalino Watch.
t.Semmerholm: Heroes for the Summer Tourney were to be selected at the Forest of Affray in Axmure, with Hayaak choosing five people to organise teams.
t.Sermersuaq: Thule ritual magic was to destroy a Jotun fortification at Pyhatunturi, possibly reducing Cathan Canae's aid to the Jotun, while other missions supported a mithril mine raid and sought the Hylje's help.
t.Skallahn: A Skallahn spy network and preparations for a raid on the territory were being protected by conjunctions in Kallavesa and Mitwold.
t.Zenith: Zenith hosted both Sunday major battles against the Druj and several large conjunctions to exorcise lost Highguard and Urizeni souls, manipulate a winter regio and ward against winter spirits.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: At Dank Mere, a Jotun warband was to be defeated to counter Mathilda Fisher's propaganda.
r.Brocéliande/Black Boughs: A steading at the Black Hearth Wayhouse was to be defended from attack.
r.Brocéliande/Vale's Lament: Vallornspawn near a regio at Broch's Approach were to be dispersed under the Advisor on the Vallorn.
r.Casinea/Mareholm: The General of the Towerjacks was to decide how to combat the vallorn at Holmwood or Vale's Fast.
r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Several Zemress Islanders were to be rescued in the Afar Hills by the Hand of Guerra.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt: A conjunction at the Beetle Tree aimed to enable the return of Imperial soldiers.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The Yegarra and Lasambrian Jotun sought a beachhead here, and Lasambrian raiders were to be made an example of at Redhill Pastures.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: At Starkmarsh, the Imperial Spymaster was to maintain the secrecy of the Skallahn spy network.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: At Steward's Landing, the Shuttered Lantern was to hide preparations for the Skallahn raid.
r.Segura/Anduzjasse: Two rescues were planned: a magistrate lost investigating smugglers at Kabalai Campo and magicians held by the Iron Confederacy at Kalino Watch.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: The Forest of Affray was the site where heroes for the Summer Tourney were to be selected.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: A major battle at Pyhatunturi aimed to destroy a Jotun fortification with Thule magic, and a raid on a mithril mine was to be supported at Ikka's Trail.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: The Mediator of Hyljehal was to enlist the help of the Hylje at Lansipari Pines.
r.Zenith/Clypion: Clypion saw the effort to destroy Druj miasma pillars with Zakalwe's aid at the Bulwark of Lutum, alongside the exorcism of a lost Urizeni seer, manipulation of a winter regio and warding against winter spirits.
r.Zenith/Iteri: The Master of the School of Exorcism was to exorcise a fallen Highguard Exarch at the Ceramic Meander.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Imperial forces were to intercept ghulai bringing vital resources to the Tainted Basilisk ritualists at the Fields of Resplendent Twilight.

Splitting the pot.d: After the Synod condemned Whittle's Hatred sect, General Ciaphas 'Black Jack' Dekar ordered the Bounders to encircle Whittle, admitting only Marcher magistrates and militia. Short-handed, Magistrate Cooper negotiated for a week without success. He then deputised two hundred and fifty Bounders and advanced. In the Battle of Whittle Hill more than two-thirds of the Whittlers died, along with thirty-three Bounders and sixteen militia. The three surviving condemned were tried, and investigators found many villagers had been anointed with auras of Hatred using stockpiled liao. Whittle is now a ghost town, and the Mournwold remained calm. The legality of Dekar's actions remains an open question.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Whittlers resented that they had been condemned through the actions of the Dawnish Cardinal of Vigilance.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Whittlers credited their Hatred of the Jotun with sustaining their resistance during the occupation, and accused the Marchers of doing the Jotun's work.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: passing Navarr are named as people a magistrate might normally have recruited to help, had outsiders not been barred.
n.The League: Tassato militia rounded up the Whittler enclave of Little Mournwold and its alder Margaret Steward was executed. The Marchers there are leaving, League citizens are moving in, and the flow of Mournwold green iron to Tassato's businesses has ended.
n.The Marches: Marcher soldiers and militia fought and killed fellow Marchers at Whittle, wiping out the condemned sect at heavy cost. Most Marchers blamed the Whittlers for their fate, but General Dekar's conduct remains contested.

t.Mournwold: The village of Whittle was besieged and stormed, leaving it an empty ghost town with orphans rehomed and an orchard planted over the graves. The wider territory stayed calm despite shock at the violence.
t.Tassato: The Little Mournwold enclave was broken up with little resistance and is being abandoned to League citizens, ending its trade in Mournwold green iron.

r.Mournwold/Green March: Whittle was encircled by the Bounders and largely destroyed in the Battle of Whittle Hill. Its leaders, priests and many young defenders were killed and the village left deserted.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: A few hundred Tassato militia seized the Whittler enclave here and executed alder Margaret Steward. The remaining Marchers are leaving and the city is reclaiming their homes.

Struggle with the sea.d: Finna i Fijadoz i Guerra's Winter mandate urged the Freeborn to abandon Feroz, and many from Afarjasse and Morajasse fled into Madruga and Segura, where kin, Zemress islanders and priests of the Little Mother took them in. Those in the Cazar Straits, Fontargenta and Oranseri had no such right, and Grendel at Mora's Rock now arrest anyone near the border. Imperial military units and fleets could stealthily evacuate them, raising taxes in Segura and Madruga and hurting Rahab's profits. Further options included a Synod mandate allowing open fighting at the cost of a diplomatic incident, aid from the Commonwealth and Asavean priests in Oran, a Sarcophan ritual, and a rescue of two stranded Zemress islanders. Rocio's 'Feroz is waiting' statement had no effect.

n.Grendel: The Grendel now fully control Feroz and Spiral and have sealed the Feroz border, but Governor Rahab stands to lose much of his profit if the evacuation succeeds, and a bolder Imperial approach would provoke a diplomatic incident and Grendel demands for reparations.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn heeded their Assembly's mandate to abandon Feroz, taking in refugees through ties of kin and tribe, and Freeborn fleets were offered the chance to smuggle the remaining countryfolk out by sea, while the Assembly could choose to sanction open fighting.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Brother of Wizards asked that the Sarcophan covert-fleet ritual be made part of Imperial or Urizen lore before the end of the year.

t.Feroz: Fully under Grendel rule, Feroz saw much of its western population flee and its borders sealed, with a covert operation offered to rescue the many still trapped and so permanently reduce the territory's taxation revenue for its holder.
t.Madruga: Madruga received refugees fleeing by land and would host most of those evacuated by sea, bringing short-term disruption but potentially raising its taxation by up to 30 Thrones a season and offering new vineyards and coastal towns.
t.Segura: Segura took in Freeborn crossing from western Feroz, with Zemress islanders offering work on their fields; a successful overland evacuation could raise its taxation by up to 20 Thrones a season and bring herb garden expertise.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral was noted as now wholly Grendel-held, with Salt Lord Kaliact apparently more interested in undisturbed access to the Legacy than in profit.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Many Freeborn fled Afarjasse into Madruga and Segura, but some remain, and the Zemress islanders Mira and Ira were trapped in its western woods, hunted by Grendel patrols, with a Sentinel Gate rescue offered from the Afar Hills.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The corsair families of the Cazar Straits were among those barred from leaving by land, but their coastline made them the likeliest to be evacuated wholesale by Imperial fleets.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Freeborn in Fontargenta were trapped under Grendel rule, needing both overland escorts and sea evacuation, and rescued vintners and agricultural specialists could found new vineyards in Madruga.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Many Freeborn left Morajasse for Segura, but Grendel soldiers garrisoning Mora's Rock have now sealed the border and arrest those near it, leaving the stragglers needing Imperial military escort.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: As a Grendel stronghold, Oranseri's port towns held many trapped Freeborn who would be the hardest to evacuate, though a full sea evacuation could bring them to swell Madruga's coastal towns.

The Queen's door.d: Eleonaris cannot refuse a Knights of Glory summons, but she had threatened to aid the Empire's enemies if it was cast again, so the Empire stopped using it. Words of thanks would no longer suffice; a Senate commission was needed. The safe option was a folly ceded to her, ideally at Semmer's Rose, costing 30 wains of white granite and 60 crowns. Alternatively, a fane (10 wains of mithril, 10 rings of ilium, 20 crowns), based on a design by the executed sorcerer Arvandor the White, could be built at the Giltmere or Oremont, winning her approval. A fane at the Semmerstones would make her withdraw support from the Jotun but enrage Meraud, Cathan Canae and Jaheris.

n.Dawn: Three of the four proposed sites lay in Dawnish lands: a folly at Semmer's Rose or a fane at the Semmerstones in Semmerholm, or a fane at the Giltmere near Weaving in Astolat. The fane design itself came from the Dawnish enchanter Arvandor the White.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Llofir's garden in Highguard's Reikos was cited as an example of an eternal building on a site ceded to it.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were revealed to have ceded fanes to most Summer eternals, which is how they secured Eleonaris' aid against the Empire; ceding her the Semmerstones would persuade her to withdraw that support.
n.Wintermark: Oremont, a mountain in Wintermark's Northspires, was identified as a possible site for a fane ceded to Eleonaris, an alternative to giving up Dawnish land.

t.Astolat: The Giltmere, a regio near Weaving claimed by Eleonaris and home to a legendary burning ram, was proposed as a site for a fane, which would mean ceding it and the surrounding hills to her.
t.Hahnmark: Oremont in Hahnmark was proposed as a site for a fane to Eleonaris, ceding the mountain regio to her and allowing her heralds to move freely through the region.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Llofir's garden in Reikos was given as a precedent for an eternal building on a ceded site.
t.Semmerholm: Semmer's Rose was the civil service's preferred site for the safe folly option, while ceding a fane at the Semmerstones would hand Eleonaris one of the Empire's greatest Summer regios and enrage Meraud, Cathan Canae and Jaheris.

r.Hahnmark/Northspires: Oremont, an orichalcum-rich peak in Northspires with ancient ruins and rumoured gryphons, was proposed as a fane site whose warding would let Eleonaris' heralds come and go throughout the region.

The bird and the child.d: Yaw'nagrah agreed to parley at the Cwllwch Stone in Liathaven, reached via the Sentinel Gate. Phaleron refused a parley in anger that the Gift of Knowledge had been placed in Imperial lore, offering contact only through the Emissary to the Celestial Library. Sinokenon sought talks on the Imperial Orcs. Prospero accepted, proposing permanent patronage of the Urizeni heliopticon college and seeking tourney champions. Wise Rangara accepted, bringing an emissary of Blood-on-the-Snow. Cathan Canae accepted, sending a champion to challenge Wintermark. Lashonar arranged a Caucus Forum meeting with the Sentinels of the Lambent Claw and a contest of words in the Imperial Regio. The Civil Service warned that dealings with eternals under enmity risk treason.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage of Spring who will lead the parley with Yaw'nagrah is Ser Fabienne De Miel of Dawn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Wise Rangara notes the Empire is beset by the Druj, and the Sentinels of the Lambent Claw are described as fighting the Druj.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage of Summer, who receives Cathan Canae's emissary, is Exarch Luke of Highguard.
n.Imperial Orcs: Sinokenon invited the Archmage of Day to bring up to half a dozen orcs, ideally including magicians such as the Weigher of Worth and a representative of their national assembly, to a parley focused on the challenges facing their nation.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae's emissary wishes to hear from battle mages who have bested Jotun warriors, in battle or otherwise.
n.Urizen: Phaleron rebuked the Empire over the Gift of Knowledge leaving Urizen's control, while Prospero offered permanent patronage of the new Urizeni college and Lashonar invited three Urizen to meet the Sentinels of the Lambent Claw, possibly involving Herminius of House of the Wanderer.
n.Wintermark: Cathan Canae's champion Barag Glacier-Splitter was to undertake a Threefold Challenge with the people of Wintermark, and Blood-on-the-Snow's emissary asked that up to three Wintermark citizens, preferably icewalkers, attend Wise Rangara's parley.

t.Liathaven: Yaw'nagrah agreed to parley at the Cwllwch Stone within the vallorn of Liathaven, sending the Old One of Liathaven, some Heirs of Terunael and children of her own.
t.Sermersuaq: The emissary of Blood-on-the-Snow attending Wise Rangara's parley wishes to discuss recent events in Sermersuaq with Winterfolk.
t.Zenith: Lashonar arranged for representatives of the Sentinels of the Lambent Claw, Zenith folk who have embraced a dangerous word-forging power to fight the Druj, to meet the Archmage of Night seeking a compromise.

r.Liathaven/Liath's Heart: A Sentinel Gate conjunction to the Cwllwch Stone in Liath's Heart opens for half an hour on the Friday evening, allowing no more than 26 people to travel to the parley with Yaw'nagrah's agents.

Tired of sleeping.d: Following Skywise Gralka's mandate, captains from every nation reached Kantor, Issyk and Maykop and found the former orc slaves already waiting, guided by dreams of ancestral voices. Several thousand Tamazi, a single extended family who honour ancestor bones and dragonbone, were settling in Skarsind, many joining the Imperial Orcs. Some practise secret ancestral magic, and their bonecarvers hold rituals but have not yet joined the nation. Hundreds wanted to attend the College of Warcasting, which would need a Senate-commissioned expansion. Their beliefs about the Howling Abyss may concern the Synod. Imperial fleets trading with Kantor or Issyk faced a 3 rank penalty. Talk also turned to a 60th anniversary festival and Varushkan amends.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: one Dawnish captain joined the rescue, a Dawnish sailor's joke spread through the fleet, and a few human former slaves may settle in Dawn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Axou feared freed orcs might spy for the Druj, whom they mostly fight, and the Druj are named among those who once enslaved defeated enemies.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Axou feared freed orcs might serve the Grendel, and orcs once subject to the Grendel are contrasted with the Tamazi.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: six Highborn captains are listed among those who sailed to Axos.
n.Imperial Orcs: Their mandate brought several thousand Tamazi to Skarsind, many of whom joined the nation. It also raised questions about expanding the College of Warcasting, how the Assembly should approach Tamazi beliefs, and how to mark the nation's 60th anniversary at the Autumn Equinox.
n.Navarr: Navarri captains made a particularly strong showing in the voyage to Axos, with around eighteen listed among those who carried refugees away.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn captains made up the largest contingent of the rescue fleets, and many of the human former slaves are expected to make new lives on the Brass Coast.
n.The League: League captains joined the voyage, most of the human former slaves are expected to settle in the League, and Sarvos ox-cart vendors profited from the orcs' overland journey.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: three Marcher captains took part, and Marcher farms are named among those once worked by orc slaves.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are named among the antecedents of the Imperial Orcs who enslaved defeated enemies in wars with Varushka.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: five Urizen captains took part, Urizen is noted to have kept slaves, and the Ambassador to Axos is Tarquinius of Urizen.
n.Varushka: A Varushkan statement calling for orc remains to be returned to Skarsind prompted debate over the dangers of disturbing graves. It also raised the suggestion that resource-rich Varushka might instead make amends by funding the Illarawm ossuary or another sept project.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: ten Wintermark captains took part, a few human former slaves may settle there, and its farms are named among those once worked by orc slaves.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the human former slaves were keen to reach the Bay of Catazar on the voyage from Axos.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Commonwealth captains who came to visit the Empire were left well placed to help evacuate Feroz should the call come.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the former soldiers and gladiators of Mareave are contrasted with the Tamazi.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the septs of Ossium are contrasted with the Tamazi, who are far less resistant to joining the Imperial Orcs.
t.Sarvos: Ox-cart vendors in Sarvos did a roaring trade in the month after the first Tamazi arrived, carrying them on their overland trek.
t.Skarsind: Several thousand Tamazi were settling across Skarsind, many in Gildenheim, offered sanctuary there by Imperial Orc reavers and preachers. The territory was also suggested as the resting place for repatriated orc remains, possibly in the Illarawm's proposed ossuary.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: caravans heading towards Temeschwar were swollen with orcs on their way to Skarsind.

r.Skarsind/Estermark: Several hundred Tamazi petitioned to attend the College of Warcasting in Estermark, which would need a likely Senate-backed expansion costing 12 wains of weirwood and 24 crowns over three months. In return, Tamazi artisans would supply warcaster items to the Preceptor.

To see what you sell.d: A Prosperity mandate prompted a proposal to restore the Elos docks in Redoubt: 35 wains of weirwood, 35 of white granite and 140 crowns over six months, to be commissioned by the end of 384YE. The docks could later be cheaply expanded into a shipyard, possibly hidden from the Grendel. The Sand Fishers studied in Holberg, trained with House Remys, at Skarsind's School of Warcasting, as scriveners and on the Navarr trods. They resolved to log Misericorde and Utterlund once they had bought the materials themselves. The Freeborn were urged to create a Prosperity festival by Spring 385YE. A tomb apparently belonging to the forgotten exemplar Badir i Durr i Riqueza was found near Rojota.

n.Dawn: House Remys offered to teach magic to the Sand Fishers, and the young winter-adept White Breath travelled alone to Dawn to study necromancy under Enchantress Claudia Remys.
n.Druj: The Sand Fishers studied and armed themselves to resist the Druj, but declined to spy on them because they refused to endure the miasma again; Urizeni refugees from the Druj invasion of Zenith were swelling Redoubt.
n.Grendel: The Elos docks would be commercial and could not legitimately be called a breach of the peace treaty, but the Grendel would recognise the threat. Any later shipyard there could be veiled from Grendel spies by the Penumbral Watcher.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs' offer to teach battle magic was taken up, cautiously, by more than thirty Sand Fishers. They came to Skarsind's School of Warcasting despite their wariness of other orc tribes.
n.Jotun: Three Lasambrian Jotun armies were advancing on Rojota and threatening all of Gambit, though they were thought unlikely to desecrate the newly found tomb.
n.Navarr: In response to the Navarr Assembly's invitation, more than a dozen Sand Fishers began walking the trods. They stayed at Navarr wayhouses and insisted on working for their board.
n.The Brass Coast: A mandate stirred the Freeborn to found a new festival honouring Zemress and Prosperity, ideally at the Spring Equinox of 385YE. A proposal was also made to mark Broken Wheel participants with white headscarves. A handful of Sand Fishers apprenticed as scriveners, and a tomb of the lost exemplar Badir i Durr i Riqueza was discovered.
n.The League: The League National Assembly's list of ways to repay the Empire drew the warmest response from the Sand Fishers. It led to their plan to improve Holberg's lands and boost Senate revenue.
n.Urizen: Restoring Elos could double Redoubt's shipping capacity, reward Urizeni fleets based there and raise taxes. It might even let Urizen support a navy alongside the Citadel Guard.

t.Bay of Catazar: Trade in the Bay had grown greatly since the peace treaty with the Grendel, but the treaty forbade the Empire to build a shipyard on it. That made any veiled shipyard at Elos a sensitive prospect.
t.Holberg: Sand Fishers were increasingly seen attending the city's university and schools at the Senate's expense. They also planned to sell timber in Holberg to raise the territory's wealth and taxation.
t.Kahraman: Soldiers skirmishing with Lasambrian raiders discovered a buried tomb with a potent Prosperity-like aura, apparently belonging to the forgotten exemplar Badir i Durr i Riqueza.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt was offered the restoration of the old naval port of Elos, which would relieve its congested ports, increase taxation by 10 thrones a season and benefit refugees. The offer lapsed if the work was not commissioned by the end of 384YE.
t.Segura: The Zemress Islanders settled in Segura pressed for a more uplifting celebration than the Feast of the Broken Wheel, sparking the Freeborn debate over a new Prosperity festival.
t.Skarsind: More than thirty Sand Fishers arrived at the Skarsind School of Warcasting to learn battle magic so they could fight the Druj.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel conquest of Spiral sent Urizeni refugees to Redoubt and left Redoubt as Urizen's only coastline.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni refugees fleeing the Druj invasion of Zenith had settled in Redoubt.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Sand Fishers planned to build sawmills and log Misericorde's forests to create profitable woodland preserves. They would buy the 15 wains each of mithril and weirwood at the Misericorde Market, which would take at least two years.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Utterlund's forests were included in the Sand Fishers' logging plan, which aimed to tame the woods into well-managed, profitable woodland.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The tomb was found a day or so south-west of Rojota, in grasslands that the advancing Lasambrian Jotun might control by the end of the Spring Equinox, which made any expedition difficult.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Mentioned in passing: Naris is not named on the page, which concerns Redoubt's ports at Elos, Cargo and Visten in general.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: Mentioned in passing: Optarion is not named on the page, which concerns Redoubt's ports at Elos, Cargo and Visten in general.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Mentioned in passing: the destruction of the Apulus docks diverted shipping to Redoubt's ports.

Watches from the Wall.d: The Wisdom Assembly (338-0) and League Assembly (312-0) endorsed the consecration. Holberg's residents then reported vivid dreams and unexplained dedications to Wisdom. Several opportunities followed. Until the end of the Winter Solstice 384YE, the Cardinal of Wisdom may enact a Focus of Wisdom mandate (25 liao) urging the faithful to solve a named problem. Reducing the Walls of Holberg would destroy the auras, but students proposed barbicans (100 wains of white granite, 200 crowns) raising its strength to 15,000. The Senate could trade one historical research capacity for an extra appraisal. Upgrading the Towerjacks to Engineer quality would cost 50 mithril and 100 crowns, which the Senate approved; this remains open until Spring Equinox 385YE. Holmauer Park's blight remains unresolved.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the orcs are cited as Holberg's relentless attackers for decades, justifying the proposed expansion of the city's defences.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard's great libraries are compared to Holberg's, and two Highborn visitors dreamed of being aboard a ship with Atun.
n.The League: The League's priests backed the consecration unanimously, and the Senate voted to upgrade the Towerjacks, one of the League's two armies, to Engineer quality. Proposals to strengthen Holberg's walls and to move civil servants to the city are also open.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's great libraries are noted as something Holberg lacks a rival to.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: a visiting boyar from Miekarova was the first to notice the second aura over the Holmauer Gate.

t.Holberg: The city gained two enduring auras of Wisdom, and its residents experienced visionary dreams and spontaneous dedications. Its walls can no longer be reduced without destroying the auras, though a costly upgrade to 15,000 strength has been proposed. The blight on Holmauer Park remains.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: a boyar visiting from Miekarova first remarked on the miraculous aura over the gate.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: The Holmauer Gate gallery became a consecrated, lit and painted gathering place for scholars, with a second aura over the gate beneath. Holmauer Park still suffers the Hag Queen's blight, which residents hope the new initiatives might address.

With a flower, with a flame.d: At the Winter Solstice, the Voices of the Unbound Storm raised a castle of ice and granite in Kalpamark, while the Sussivari Frost Coven and the Moon and Stars raised four castles of mist over fens and marshes in Bregasland and Kallavesa. The Penumbral Veil moved from Ossium and Semmerholm to Madruga and Kahraman. A star settled atop the White City's highest basilica after a vision of a veiled procession. Basileus Flint, Lashonar, Surut and Barien announced games, contests and bargains. Eternals recruited champions for a Summer tourney for the Icy Crag. Hayaak offered trials in the Forest of Affray via Axmure, and Meraud sought the Celestial Arch's help rescuing magicians at Kalino Tower.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish coven Moon and Stars helped raise castles of mist in Bregasland and Kallavesa, and the darkness over Semmerholm lifted. Dawn's Glory Square was named as the stage for Barien's preaching tournament and Meraud's contest, while the Forest of Affray trials ran through a regio in Axmure.
n.Highguard: Bastion witnessed a vast silent light show that ended with a glowing star resting atop the White City's highest basilica for the season. The Highborn magister Ahzrukhal son of Night was also named as Sadogua's sole champion for the Summer tourney.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Eternal Family of Navarr was among five candidates invited by Hayaak to form a team for his Forest of Affray trials.
n.The Brass Coast: The Penumbral Veil settled over the Freeborn territories of Madruga and Kahraman. Fleeing Suranni magicians were seeking sanctuary in southern Segura, and Meraud's Freeborn friends offered to help them across the border if they were rescued.
n.The Marches: Castles of mist were raised over the fens of the Rushes and Ottermire in Bregasland, adding magical fortifications to the Marcher territory.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Sejanus of Urizen was named as the surviving member of Adamant's team for the Summer tourney and was asked to find new companions.
n.Varushka: The inky black night skies that had hung over Ossium dissipated as the Penumbral Veil moved to the Brass Coast.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark magicians raised a castle of ice in Hahnmark and castles of mist in Kallavesa and Bregasland. Barien extended his challenge to the Ice Walkers to the Summer Solstice, and the Voices of the Unbound Storm were invited to Hayaak's trials.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat itself is not named, though the Glory Square 'of Dawn' was set as a venue for Barien's and Meraud's contests.
t.Bastion: A magical display of stars and veiled figures filled the night sky over Bastion, leaving a glowing star atop the White City's tallest basilica spire for the season.
t.Bregasland: Castles of mist were raised over the fens of the Rushes and Ottermire, fortifying the territory with magic.
t.Hahnmark: A great castle of ice and granite drawn from the Breath of Winter was raised in the hills of Kalpamark.
t.Kahraman: The Penumbral Veil now hung over Kahraman, shrouding the territory.
t.Kalino: Kalino Tower, a watchtower on the Brass Coast's southern border, was the destination of a conjunction in which Imperial magicians were asked to rescue renegade magicians from Arav's priesthood.
t.Kallavesa: Castles of mist were raised over West Marsh and Kallavesa Marsh by Wintermark and Dawnish covens.
t.Madruga: The Penumbral Veil now hung over Madruga, shrouding the territory.
t.Ossium: The inky black night skies that had covered Ossium dissipated.
t.Segura: Renegade Suranni magicians fleeing Arav's priesthood were trying to cross from Arbonne into the sanctuary of southern Segura.
t.Semmerholm: The black night skies over Semmerholm cleared, and a regio in Axmure became the route to the Forest of Affray for Hayaak's trials.

r.Bregasland/Ottermire: A castle of mist was raised over the fens of Ottermire.
r.Hahnmark/Kalpamark: The Voices of the Unbound Storm raised a great castle of ice and granite in the hills of Kalpamark.
r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: A castle of mist was raised over Kallavesa Marsh.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: A castle of mist was raised over the marshes of West Marsh.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: A Summer regio in Axmure, opened by Barien, gave access to the Forest of Affray for those bearing Hayaak's token.
